title.zh: 卷一百二十一 志第七十四 禮二十四
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 志第七十四 禮二十四 Volume 121 Treatises 74: Rites 24

sentences.zh: 禮二十四

translations.literal: Rites 24
translations.idiomatic: Rites 24

sentences.zh: （軍禮）〉

translations.literal: (Military Rites)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Military Rites)〉

sentences.zh: ○祃祭閱武受降獻俘田獵打球救日伐鼓

translations.literal: ○ Ma sacrifice, military review, accepting surrender, presenting captives, field hunting, cuju ball game, rescuing the sun, beating drums
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ma sacrifice; military reviews; accepting surrender and presenting captives; field hunts; cuju; rituals to rescue the sun; and drum-beating

sentences.zh: 祃，師祭也，宜居軍禮之首。

translations.literal: Ma is the army sacrifice; it properly should stand first among military rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ma sacrifice was the army's ritual offering and rightly belonged at the head of military rites.

sentences.zh: 講武次之，受降、獻俘又次之。

translations.literal: Military exercises came next; accepting surrender and presenting captives came after that.
translations.idiomatic: Martial drills followed, with accepting surrender and presenting captives ranked after them.

sentences.zh: 田獵以下，亦各以類附焉。

translations.literal: Field hunting and below were likewise grouped by category.
translations.idiomatic: Field hunting and the rites below it were likewise arranged by kind.

sentences.zh: 軍前大旗曰牙，師出必祭，謂之祃。

translations.literal: The great banner before the army was called the ya; when the army set out it had to be sacrificed to—this was called ma.
translations.idiomatic: The main army banner was called the ya banner; whenever troops marched out they had to sacrifice to it, and this was called the ma rite.

sentences.zh: 後魏出師，又建纛頭旗上。

translations.literal: When the Later Wei sent out troops, they also erected a banner with a tassel head above it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Wei took the field they also set up a great standard topped with a tassel head.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，出京前一日，遣右贊善大夫潘慎修出郊，用少牢一祭蚩尤、祃牙；

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned in Hedong, on the day before leaving the capital he sent Right Assistant Gentleman Pan Shenxiu to the suburbs to offer one shao-lao sacrifice to Chiyou and to perform the ma rite for the ya banner;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Hedong, on the eve of his departure from the capital he sent Right Assistant Gentleman Pan Shenxiu outside the city to offer a shao-lao victim to Chiyou and perform the ma rite for the ya banner;

sentences.zh: 遣著作佐郎李巨源即北郊望氣壇用香、柳枝、燈油、乳粥、酥蜜餅、果，祭北方天王。

translations.literal: He sent Assistant Compiler Li Juyuan to the Qi-observation altar in the northern suburbs to offer incense, willow branches, lamp oil, milk porridge, honey cakes, and fruit in sacrifice to the Northern Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Assistant Compiler Li Juyuan to the qi-watching altar in the northern suburbs with incense, willow branches, lamp oil, milk porridge, honey cakes, and fruit to sacrifice to the Northern Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，詔太常禮院定祃儀。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, an edict ordered the Directorate of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix the ma rite.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping reign an edict directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to establish the ma ritual.

sentences.zh: 所司除地為壇，兩壝繞以青繩，張幄帟，置軍牙、六纛位版。

translations.literal: The responsible office cleared ground for an altar, encircled the two embankments with blue cord, hung curtains, and set up tablets for the army ya and the six great banners.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office cleared ground for an altar, ringed the double embankments with blue cord, hung curtains, and set out tablets marking the places of the army ya and the six great banners.

sentences.zh: 版方七寸，厚和三分。

translations.literal: The tablets were seven inches square, three fen thick in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each tablet was seven inches square and three fen thick overall.

sentences.zh: 祭用剛日，具饌。

translations.literal: The sacrifice used a gang day; provisions were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was performed on a gang day, with full offerings prepared.

sentences.zh: 牲用大牢，以羊豕代。

translations.literal: Victims were to be da-lao, but sheep and pigs were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: The prescribed victim was the da-lao, though sheep and pigs were used in its place.

sentences.zh: 其幣長 一丈八尺，軍牙以白，六纛以皂。

translations.literal: The silk offerings were one zhang and eight chi long; white for the army ya, black for the six great banners.
translations.idiomatic: The silk offerings were one zhang and eight chi long—white for the army ya and black for the six great banners.

sentences.zh: 都部署初獻，副都部署亞獻，部署三獻，皆戎服，清齋一宿。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief made the primary offering, the deputy commander the secondary, and a deployment commander the tertiary; all wore military dress and fasted in purification for one night.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief made the primary offering, the deputy commander the secondary, and a deployment commander the tertiary; all wore military dress and kept a night of ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 將校陪位。

translations.literal: Generals and officers attended in supporting places.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and officers stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 禮畢焚幣，釁鼓以一牢。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished the silk was burned and the drums smeared with blood from one victim.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended the silk offerings were burned and the drums anointed with blood from a single victim.

sentences.zh: 又擇日祭馬祖、馬社。

translations.literal: On another chosen day they sacrificed to the Horse Ancestor and the Horse Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day they also sacrificed to the Horse Ancestor and the Horse Altar.

sentences.zh: 閱武，仍前代制。

translations.literal: Military review still followed the institutions of earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Military reviews still followed the institutions of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗征伐四方，親講武事，故不盡用定儀，亦不常其處。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong campaigned in all directions and personally directed martial exercises, so they did not fully use the fixed ritual and did not keep to one place.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taizu and Taizong campaigned in every direction and personally directed martial drills, they did not always follow the fixed ritual and did not always hold reviews in the same place.

sentences.zh: 鑿講武池朱明門外以習水戰。

translations.literal: They cut a martial-exercise pool outside the Vermilion Bright Gate to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They excavated a drill pool outside the Vermilion Bright Gate to practice naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 復築講武台城西楊村，秋九月大閱，與從臣登臺觀焉。

translations.literal: They also built a martial-exercise terrace at Yang Village west of the city; in the ninth month of autumn they held a great review, and with their attending ministers they ascended the terrace to watch.
translations.idiomatic: They also built a drill terrace at Yang Village west of the city, and in the ninth month of autumn held a grand review at which they and their attending ministers mounted the terrace to watch.

sentences.zh: 真宗詔有司擇地含輝門外之東武村為廣場，馮高為台，臺上設屋，構行宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong ordered the responsible offices to choose ground at Dongwu Village outside the Splendid Radiance Gate as an open field, pile it high into a terrace, set a building on the terrace, and construct a traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong ordered officials to select ground at Dongwu Village outside the Splendid Radiance Gate as a parade ground, raise a high terrace, place a pavilion upon it, and build a traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 其夜三鼓，殿前、侍衛馬步諸軍分出諸門。

translations.literal: That night at the third drum the Palace Front and Imperial Guard horse and foot armies issued forth through the gates.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch the Palace Front and Imperial Guard horse and foot units marched out through the city gates.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，帝乘馬，從官並戎服，賜以窄袍。

translations.literal: At dawn the emperor mounted a horse; his attending officials all wore military dress and were granted narrow-sleeved robes.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor rode out on horseback; his attendants all wore military dress and were given narrow-sleeved robes.

sentences.zh: 至 行宮，諸軍陣台前，左右相向，步騎交屬亙二十裡，諸班衛士翼從於後。

translations.literal: Arriving at the traveling palace, the armies formed before the terrace facing one another left and right; foot and horse interlinked for twenty li; the various guard companies flanked and followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the traveling palace the armies formed before the terrace, facing one another on left and right, with infantry and cavalry interlinked for twenty li while the various guard companies flanked and followed behind.

sentences.zh: 有司奏成列，帝升台東向，禦戎帳，召從臣坐觀之。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported that the ranks were formed; the emperor ascended the terrace facing east, took his seat in a military tent, and summoned his attending ministers to sit and watch.
translations.idiomatic: When the responsible office reported that the ranks were formed, the emperor mounted the terrace facing east, took his seat in a military tent, and summoned his ministers to sit and watch.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使王超執五方旗以節進退， 又於兩陣中起候台相望，使人執旗如臺上之數以相應。

translations.literal: Palace Front Commander-in-Chief Wang Chao held the five-direction flags to regulate advance and retreat; signal platforms were also raised between the two formations facing one another, and men held flags matching those on the terrace to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Commander-in-Chief Wang Chao held the five-direction flags to regulate advance and retreat; signal platforms were also raised between the two formations, and men with flags matching those on the terrace coordinated the movements.

sentences.zh: 初舉黃旗，諸軍旅拜。

translations.literal: When the yellow flag was first raised, the armies bowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow flag was first raised, the armies bowed.

sentences.zh: 舉赤旗則騎進，舉青旗則步進。

translations.literal: Raising the red flag made the cavalry advance; raising the green flag made the infantry advance.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the red flag sent the cavalry forward; raising the green flag sent the infantry forward.

sentences.zh: 每旗動則鼓駴士噪，聲震百裡外，皆三挑乃退。

translations.literal: Whenever a flag moved the drums rolled and the soldiers shouted; the sound shook the countryside a hundred li away; each unit charged three times before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a flag moved the drums rolled and the soldiers shouted until the sound shook the countryside a hundred li away; each unit charged three times before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 次舉白 旗，諸軍復再拜，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Next the white flag was raised; the armies bowed again and shouted "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Next the white flag was raised; the armies bowed again and shouted "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 有司奏陣堅而整，士勇而厲，欲再舉，詔止之，遂舉黑旗以振旅。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported that the formations were firm and orderly and the soldiers brave and sharp; they wished to raise the flags again, but an edict stopped them, and then the black flag was raised to dismiss the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office reported that the formations were firm and orderly and the soldiers brave and sharp; they wished to run another round, but the emperor ordered them to stop, and the black flag was raised to dismiss the troops.

sentences.zh: 軍于左者略右陣以還，由台前出西北隅；

translations.literal: The army on the left skirted the right formation to return and passed out through the northwest corner before the terrace;
translations.idiomatic: The army on the left skirted the right formation to return and marched out through the northwest corner before the terrace;

sentences.zh: 軍于右者略左陣以還，由台前 出西南隅，並凱旋以退。

translations.literal: the army on the right skirted the left formation to return and passed out through the southwest corner before the terrace; both withdrew in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: the army on the right skirted the left formation to return and marched out through the southwest corner before the terrace; both withdrew in triumph.

sentences.zh: 乃召從臣宴，教坊奏樂。

translations.literal: Then he summoned his attending ministers to a feast, and the Music Office performed.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned his ministers to a feast while the Music Office performed.

sentences.zh: 回禦東華門，閱諸軍還營，鈞容奏樂於樓下，復召從臣坐，賜飲。

translations.literal: Returning to the Eastern Flowery Gate, he reviewed the armies as they returned to camp; the Imperial Entertainers played music below the tower; he again summoned his attending ministers to sit and bestowed drink.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the Eastern Flowery Gate, he reviewed the armies as they returned to camp; the Imperial Entertainers played below the tower, and he again seated his ministers and bestowed drink upon them.

sentences.zh: 明日，又賜近臣飲於中書，諸軍將校飲於營中， 內職飲於軍器庫，諸班衛士飲於殿門外。

translations.literal: The next day he again bestowed drink on his close ministers at the Secretariat, on the army generals and officers in camp, on the inner service staff at the Armory, and on the various guard companies outside the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again bestowed drink on his close ministers at the Secretariat, on army generals and officers in camp, on inner-service staff at the Armory, and on the various guard companies outside the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 神宗閱左藏庫副使幵斌所教牌手於崇政殿，乃命殿前步軍司擇驍健者依法教習。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reviewed at the Chongzheng Hall the shield-bearers taught by Left Treasury Deputy Commissioner Bian Bin, and then ordered the Palace Front Foot Army Bureau to select the strongest men and train them according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong reviewed at the Chongzheng Hall the shield-bearers trained by Left Treasury Deputy Commissioner Bian Bin, then ordered the Palace Front Foot Army Bureau to select the strongest men and train them by the regulations.

sentences.zh: 自是，營屯及更戍諸軍、畿甸 三路民兵皆隨伎藝召見親閱焉。

translations.literal: From this time on, garrison troops, rotating frontier armies, and the three-circuit militia of the capital region were all summoned for personal review according to their skills.
translations.idiomatic: From then on garrison troops, rotating frontier armies, and the three-circuit militia of the capital region were all summoned for personal review according to their skills.

sentences.zh: 凡閱試禁衛、戍軍、民兵，總率第其精角，賜以金帛；

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial guards, frontier troops, and militia were reviewed and tested, their leaders were ranked by excellence and given gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial guards, frontier troops, and militia were reviewed, their leaders were ranked by excellence and rewarded with gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 而超等高者，至命為吏選官，其典領者優加職秩。

translations.literal: those of highest rank such as Chao were even appointed to office through clerk selection; those who commanded them received preferential advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: the highest performers, such as Chao, were even appointed to office through clerk selection, while their commanders received preferential advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 涇原經略蔡挺肄習諸將軍 馬，點閱周悉，隊伍有法，入為樞密副使，因言於上而引試之。

translations.literal: Jingyuan Military Commissioner Cai Ting drilled the generals in horsemanship; his inspections were thorough and his formations disciplined; entering office as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he spoke to the throne and had them brought for trial review.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan Military Commissioner Cai Ting drilled the generals in horsemanship; his inspections were thorough and his formations disciplined. After he entered office as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he spoke to the throne and had the troops brought for trial review.

sentences.zh: 舊以七軍營陣校試，而分數不齊，前後牴牾。

translations.literal: Formerly the seven armies' camp formation commanders were tested, but their scores were uneven and contradicted one another.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the seven armies' camp formation commanders were tested, but their scores were uneven and contradicted one another.

sentences.zh: 命校試官采掇定為八軍法。

translations.literal: The review officials were ordered to gather and fix an Eight Armies method.
translations.idiomatic: The review officials were ordered to gather and fix an Eight Armies method.

sentences.zh: 及軍法成，頒行諸路。

translations.literal: When the army method was complete, it was promulgated to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When the army method was complete, it was promulgated to all circuits.

sentences.zh: 既又 定九軍法，以一軍營陣，即城南好草披閱之，皆有賞賚。

translations.literal: Later the Nine Armies method was also fixed; one army's camp formation was reviewed on the good grass south of the city, and rewards were given in every case.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Nine Armies method was also established; one army's camp formation was reviewed on the good grass south of the city, and rewards were given in every case.

sentences.zh: 其按閱炮場連弩及便坐日閱召募新軍時，令習戰如故事。

translations.literal: When reviewing at the artillery ground the repeating crossbows, and on informal-session days reviewing newly recruited troops, they were ordered to practice battle according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When reviewing repeating crossbows at the artillery ground, and on informal-session days when newly recruited troops were reviewed, they were ordered to practice battle according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年六月，高宗諭輔臣曰：“朕 欲親閱武。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong told his chief ministers: "I wish to review the troops in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong told his chief ministers, "I wish to review the troops in person.

sentences.zh: ”宰臣呂頤浩曰：“方右武之時，理當如此。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Lü Yihao said: "At a time when military force is paramount, this is exactly as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Lü Yihao said, "At a time when military force is paramount, this is exactly as it should be.

sentences.zh: 祖宗時不忘武備，如鑿金明池，益欲習水戰。

translations.literal: Our ancestors did not forget military preparedness; cutting the Golden Bright Pool, for example, was chiefly to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors never neglected military preparedness—for example, they cut the Golden Bright Pool chiefly to practice naval warfare.

sentences.zh: ”張浚曰：“祖宗每上巳遊，必命衛士馳射，因而激賞，亦所 以講武也。

translations.literal: " Zhang Jun said: "Whenever our ancestors went out on the third-day-of-the-third-month excursion, they always ordered the guards to shoot on horseback and rewarded them thereby—this too was a way of practicing martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun said, "Whenever our ancestors went out on the third-day-of-the-third-month excursion, they always ordered the guards to shoot on horseback and rewarded them thereby—this too was a way of keeping martial discipline.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“朕非久命諸將各閱所部人馬，當召卿等共觀，足以知諸將能否。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Before long I shall order each general to review the men and horses under his command; I shall summon you all to watch together, so that you may know whether the generals are capable.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Before long I shall order each general to review the men and horses under his command. I shall summon you all to watch together, so that you may know whether the generals are capable.

sentences.zh: ”後以巡幸，不果行。

translations.literal: " Later, because of an imperial tour, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, because of an imperial tour, the plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年正月，始禦射殿，閱諸班直殿前 司諸軍指教使臣、親從宿衛親兵並提轄部押親兵使臣射射。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Shaoxing he first attended the Archery Hall and reviewed the various guard companies, the Palace Front Bureau's army instructors, the personal attendants and inner guard close troops, and the supervising officers commanding the close troops—all shooting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Shaoxing he first attended the Archery Hall and reviewed shooting by the various guard companies, the Palace Front Bureau's army instructors, the personal attendants and inner guard close troops, and the supervising officers commanding the close troops.

sentences.zh: 共一千二百六十人，每六十人作一撥。

translations.literal: In all there were 1,260 men, every sixty forming one platoon.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were 1,260 men, every sixty forming one platoon.

sentences.zh: 遂詔戶部支金千兩，付樞密院激賞庫充犒用。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the Ministry of Revenue to disburse 1,000 taels of gold to the Bureau of Military Affairs reward treasury for consolation payments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the Ministry of Revenue to disburse 1,000 taels of gold to the Bureau of Military Affairs reward treasury for consolation payments.

sentences.zh: 三月，禦射殿，閱等 子趙青等五十人角力，轉資，支賜錢銀有差。

translations.literal: In the third month he attended the Archery Hall and reviewed fifty wrestlers including Zhao Qing; they were promoted in rank and given money and silver in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he attended the Archery Hall and reviewed fifty wrestlers including Zhao Qing; they were promoted in rank and given money and silver in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 八月，禦射殿，閱廣東路經略司解發到韶州士庶子弟陳裕試神臂弓，特補進武校尉，賜紫羅窄衫、銀束帶，差充本路經 略司指使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he attended the Archery Hall and reviewed Chen Yu, a commoner youth from Shaozhou sent up by the Guangdong Military Commission, testing the divine-arm bow; he was specially appointed Advance Martial Company Commander, granted a purple narrow-sleeved robe and silver belt, and assigned as an agent of that circuit's military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he attended the Archery Hall and reviewed Chen Yu, a commoner youth from Shaozhou sent up by the Guangdong Military Commission, as he tested the divine-arm bow; Chen was specially appointed Advance Martial Company Commander, granted a purple narrow-sleeved robe and silver belt, and assigned as an agent of that circuit's military commission.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月，閱殿前馬步軍將士藝精者，賞有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year he reviewed Palace Front horse and foot soldiers skilled in the arts; rewards varied.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year he reviewed Palace Front horse and foot soldiers skilled in the martial arts; rewards varied.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲以冬月行之，號曰冬教。

translations.literal: From this time it was held every year in the winter month and was called the Winter Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: From this time it was held every year in the winter month and was called the Winter Instruction.

sentences.zh: 三十年十月，禦射殿，引三衙統制、同統制、統領、同統領入內射 射，詔餘合赴內殿教人，依年例支降例物，令逐司自行按試等第給散

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirtieth year he attended the Archery Hall and brought in the three-commandery commanders, associate commanders, leaders, and associate leaders to shoot within the palace; an edict ordered that the remaining men due to enter the inner hall for instruction should receive the customary annual gifts by grade as each bureau tested and distributed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirtieth year he attended the Archery Hall and brought in the three-commandery commanders, associate commanders, leaders, and associate leaders to shoot within the palace; an edict ordered that the remaining men due to enter the inner hall for instruction should receive the customary annual gifts by grade as each bureau tested and distributed them

sentences.zh: （舊例，每歲引三衙官兵教。

translations.literal: (According to the old practice, each year the three commanderies' officers and soldiers were brought in for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the old practice, each year the three commanderies' officers and soldiers were brought in for instruction.

sentences.zh: 是日，止引統制、統領，故有是詔）〉

translations.literal: On this day only commanders and leaders were brought in, hence this edict.)〉
translations.idiomatic: On this day only commanders and leaders were brought in, hence this edict.)〉

sentences.zh: 三十二年四月二十五日，禦 射殿隔門特坐，引呈新舊行門射射。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month of the thirty-second year he specially sat behind the partition door of the Archery Hall and had the old and new Palace Gate guards presented for shooting.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month of the thirty-second year he specially sat behind the partition door of the Archery Hall and had the old and new Palace Gate guards presented for shooting.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年十一月，幸候潮門外大教場，次幸白石教場。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qiandao he visited the great drill ground outside the Awaiting-Tide Gate, then visited the White Stone drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qiandao he visited the great drill ground outside the Awaiting-Tide Gate, then visited the White Stone drill ground.

sentences.zh: 應從駕臣僚，自祥曦殿並戎服起居，從駕往回。

translations.literal: The officials who should accompany the imperial progress, from the Splendid Dawn Hall onward, all wore military dress for attendance and accompanied the progress there and back.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who should accompany the imperial progress, from the Splendid Dawn Hall onward, all wore military dress for attendance and accompanied the progress there and back.

sentences.zh: 內管軍、禦 帶、環衛官從駕，宰執以下免從。

translations.literal: Inner-service troops, imperial guards, and palace guard officers accompanied the progress; the chief ministers and below were excused from accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-service troops, imperial guards, and palace guard officers accompanied the progress; the chief ministers and below were excused from accompanying.

sentences.zh: 就逐幕次賜食，俟進晚膳畢，免奏萬福，並免茶，從駕還內。

translations.literal: Food was bestowed at each tent station; after the evening meal was served they were excused from reporting "Ten thousand blessings," tea was omitted, and they accompanied the progress back within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Food was bestowed at each tent station; after the evening meal was served they were excused from reporting "Long live the emperor," tea was omitted, and they accompanied the progress back within the palace.

sentences.zh: 二十四日，幸候潮門外大教場，進早膳，次幸白石教場閱兵。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day he visited the great drill ground outside the Awaiting-Tide Gate, took the morning meal, then visited the White Stone drill ground to review the troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day he visited the great drill ground outside the Awaiting-Tide Gate, took the morning meal, then visited the White Stone drill ground to review the troops.

sentences.zh: 三衙率 將佐等導駕詣白石，皇帝登臺，三衙統制、統領官等起居畢，舉黃旗，諸軍皆三呼萬歲拜訖，三衙管軍奏報取旨，馬軍上馬打圍教場。

translations.literal: The three commanderies led their generals and officers to guide the imperial progress to White Stone; the emperor ascended the terrace; after the three-commandery commanders and leader-officers had paid their respects, the yellow flag was raised and all the armies shouted "Ten thousand years!" three times and bowed; the three commanderies' army supervisors reported and received instructions; the horse army mounted and encircled the drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanderies led their generals and officers to guide the imperial progress to White Stone; the emperor mounted the terrace; after the three-commandery commanders and leader-officers had paid their respects, the yellow flag was raised and all the armies shouted "Long live the emperor!" three times and bowed; the three commanderies' army supervisors reported and received instructions; and the horse army mounted and encircled the drill ground.

sentences.zh: 舉白旗，三司馬軍首尾相接；

translations.literal: When the white flag was raised, the horse armies of the three bureaus linked head to tail;
translations.idiomatic: When the white flag was raised, the horse armies of the three bureaus linked head to tail;

sentences.zh: 舉紅旗，向台合圍，聽一金止。

translations.literal: when the red flag was raised they closed toward the terrace in a ring and halted at one stroke of the gong.
translations.idiomatic: when the red flag was raised they closed toward the terrace in a ring and halted at one stroke of the gong.

sentences.zh: 軍馬各就圍地，作圓形排立。

translations.literal: The troops and horses each took their places within the encirclement and stood in a circular formation.
translations.idiomatic: The troops and horses each took their places within the encirclement and stood in a circular formation.

sentences.zh: 射生官兵隨鼓聲出馬射獐兔，一金止。

translations.literal: The hunting archers rode out at the sound of the drum to shoot deer and hares, and halted at one stroke of the gong.
translations.idiomatic: The hunting archers rode out at the sound of the drum to shoot deer and hares, and halted at one stroke of the gong.

sentences.zh: 疊金，射生官兵各歸陣隊。

translations.literal: At repeated strokes of the gong the hunting archers each returned to their formations.
translations.idiomatic: At repeated strokes of the gong the hunting archers each returned to their formations.

sentences.zh: 舉黃旗，射生官兵就禦台下獻所獲。

translations.literal: When the yellow flag was raised the hunting archers came below the imperial terrace and presented what they had taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow flag was raised the hunting archers came below the imperial terrace and presented what they had taken.

sentences.zh: 帝遂慰勞，賜賚諸將鞍馬金帶，以及士卒。

translations.literal: The emperor then comforted and rewarded them, bestowing saddles, horses, and gold belts on the generals, and gifts on the soldiers as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then comforted and rewarded them, bestowing saddles, horses, and gold belts on the generals and gifts on the soldiers as well.

sentences.zh: 諸軍歡騰，鼓舞就列。

translations.literal: The armies rejoiced tumultuously and, beating drums, took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The armies rejoiced tumultuously and, beating drums, took their places.

sentences.zh: 百姓觀者如山。

translations.literal: The common people watching were piled like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The common people watching were piled like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 時久陰曀，暨帝出郊，雲霧解駁，風日開霽。

translations.literal: The weather had long been overcast and gloomy; when the emperor went out to the suburbs the clouds and mist broke apart and wind and sun cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The weather had long been overcast and gloomy; when the emperor went out to the suburbs the clouds and mist broke apart and wind and sun cleared.

sentences.zh: 帝遣諭主管殿前司王琪等曰：“前日 之教，師律整嚴，人無嘩囂，分合應度，朕甚悅之，皆卿等力也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent word to Palace Front Supervisor Wang Qi and others: "In the instruction of the other day the army discipline was strict and orderly, no one was noisy or disorderly, and the divisions joined and separated as they should—I am very pleased; this is all your effort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Palace Front Supervisor Wang Qi and others, "In the instruction of the other day the army discipline was strict and orderly, no one was noisy or disorderly, and the divisions joined and separated as they should—I am very pleased; this is all your effort.

sentences.zh: ”琪等曰：“此陛下神武之化，六軍恭謹所致。

translations.literal: " Qi and the others said: "This is due to Your Majesty's divine martial transformation and the six armies' respectful diligence.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi and the others said, "This is due to Your Majesty's divine martial transformation and the six armies' respectful diligence.

sentences.zh: 臣願得以此為陛下剿絕奸宄。

translations.literal: Your servants wish to use this to exterminate treacherous villains for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants wish to use this to exterminate treacherous villains for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: ” 四年 十月，殿前司言：“相視龍王堂北、江岸以東茅灘一帶平地，可作教場。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of the fourth year the Palace Front Bureau reported: "We have surveyed the level ground along Maotan east of the riverbank north of Dragon King Hall; it can serve as a drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month of the fourth year the Palace Front Bureau reported, "We have surveyed the level ground along Maotan east of the riverbank north of Dragon King Hall; it can serve as a drill ground.

sentences.zh: 已修築將壇，將來三司馬步軍並各全裝，披帶衣甲，執色器械，至日，先赴教場下方營排 辦，俟駕登臺，聽金鼓起居畢，依資次變陣教閱。

translations.literal: We have already built the general's terrace; when the day comes the horse and foot armies of the three bureaus will all be in full equipment, wearing armor and carrying colored weapons; they will first go to the drill ground below to set up camp and arrange themselves; when the imperial progress ascends the terrace they will heed the gold and drum signals for attendance, and then by seniority change formations for instructional review.
translations.idiomatic: We have already built the general's terrace; when the day comes the horse and foot armies of the three bureaus will all be in full equipment, wearing armor and carrying colored weapons; they will first go to the drill ground below to set up camp and arrange themselves; when the imperial progress ascends the terrace they will heed the gold and drum signals for attendance, and then by seniority change formations for instructional review.

sentences.zh: 所有聖駕出郊，除禁衛外，欲于本司入陣馬軍內摘差護聖馬軍八百人騎、弓箭、器械，作十六隊，於儀衛前後引 從，各分八隊，隊各五十人，往回沿路，各奏隨軍鼓笛大樂。

translations.literal: Whenever the sacred progress goes out to the suburbs, apart from the imperial guards, we wish to select from this bureau's battle-entry horse army eight hundred mounted men with bows, arrows, and weapons, formed into sixteen companies to lead and follow before and after the ceremonial guard, divided into eight companies each way, fifty men per company; going and returning along the route each will perform the army's drum, flute, and great music.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the sacred progress goes out to the suburbs, apart from the imperial guards, we wish to select from this bureau's battle-entry horse army eight hundred mounted men with bows, arrows, and weapons, formed into sixteen companies to lead and follow before and after the ceremonial guard—eight companies each way, fifty men per company; going and returning along the route each will perform the army's drum, flute, and great music.

sentences.zh: 及摘差本司入教陣隊內諸軍步親隨一千人，並統領將官三員，至日，先赴將台下，各分左右，于後壁周 圍留空地三十步，以容禁衛，外作三重環立。

translations.literal: We also wish to select from this bureau's drill-entry formations one thousand foot soldiers of the various armies' personal attendants, together with three leader-generals; on the day they will first go below the general's terrace and divide left and right; around the rear wall they will leave open ground of thirty paces to accommodate the imperial guards, and outside that stand in a triple ring.
translations.idiomatic: We also wish to select from this bureau's drill-entry formations one thousand foot soldiers of the various armies' personal attendants, together with three leader-generals; on the day they will first go below the general's terrace and divide left and right; around the rear wall they will leave open ground of thirty paces to accommodate the imperial guards, and outside that stand in a triple ring.

sentences.zh: ”十六日。

translations.literal: " On the sixteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: " On the sixteenth day.

sentences.zh: 車駕至灘上。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage arrived at the beach.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage arrived at the beach.

sentences.zh: 諸軍人馬，前一日於教場東列幕宿營。

translations.literal: The armies' men and horses had camped in tents lined up on the east of the drill ground the day before.
translations.idiomatic: The armies' men and horses had camped in tents lined up on the east of the drill ground the day before.

sentences.zh: 是日，三衙管軍與各軍統領將佐導駕乘馬至護聖步軍大 教場亭，更禦甲胄至灘上。

translations.literal: On that day the three commanderies' army supervisors and each army's leader-generals and officers guided the imperial progress on horseback to the Protect-the-Sacred Foot Army great drill-ground pavilion, then donned armor and went on to the beach.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the three commanderies' army supervisors and each army's leader-generals and officers guided the imperial progress on horseback to the Protect-the-Sacred Foot Army great drill-ground pavilion, then donned armor and went on to the beach.

sentences.zh: 皇帝登臺，三衙起居畢，權主管殿前司王逵奏三司人馬齊，舉黃旗，諸軍呼拜者三。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the terrace; after the three commanderies had paid their respects, Acting Palace Front Supervisor Wang Kui reported that the men and horses of the three bureaus were assembled; the yellow flag was raised and the armies shouted and bowed three times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the terrace; after the three commanderies had paid their respects, Acting Palace Front Supervisor Wang Kui reported that the men and horses of the three bureaus were assembled; the yellow flag was raised and the armies shouted and bowed three times.

sentences.zh: 逵奏請從頭教。

translations.literal: Kui reported and requested permission to begin instruction from the start.
translations.idiomatic: Kui reported and requested permission to begin instruction from the start.

sentences.zh: 中軍鳴角，倒門角旗出營，馬步軍簇 隊成，收鼓訖。

translations.literal: The central army sounded the horn; the gate-corner flags were reversed and the camp issued forth; horse and foot armies clustered into formations; the drums ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The central army sounded the horn; the gate-corner flags were reversed and the camp issued forth; horse and foot armies clustered into formations; and the drums ceased.

sentences.zh: 連三鼓，馬軍上馬，步人撮起旗槍。

translations.literal: Three drums in succession; the horse army mounted; the infantry raised flags and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Three successive drumbeats sounded; the cavalry mounted; the infantry raised their flags and spears.

sentences.zh: 四鼓舉白旗，中軍鼓聲旗應，變方陣為備敵之形。

translations.literal: At the fourth drum the white flag was raised; the central army's drumbeats and flags responded; the square formation changed into the form of preparing for the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth drumbeat the white flag went up; the central command's drums and flags answered in turn; and the square formation shifted into a defensive posture against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 別高一鼓，步軍四向作禦敵之勢，且戰且前，馬軍出陳作戰鬥 之勢。

translations.literal: Raising the drum once more separately, the foot army on four sides assumed a posture of repelling the enemy, advancing while fighting; the horse army issued from the formation and assumed a fighting posture.
translations.idiomatic: After one more drum signal, the infantry on all four sides took up a defensive fighting stance and pressed forward as they fought; the cavalry emerged from the formation and assumed battle positions.

sentences.zh: 別高一鼓，各分歸地分。

translations.literal: Raising the drum once more separately, each returned to his assigned sector.
translations.idiomatic: After another drum signal, each unit returned to its assigned ground.

sentences.zh: 五鼓舉黃旗，變圓陣為自環內固之形。

translations.literal: At the fifth drum the yellow flag was raised; the round formation changed into the form of self-encircling internal consolidation.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth drumbeat the yellow flag was raised; the circular formation shifted into a self-enclosing defensive ring.

sentences.zh: 如前節次訖。

translations.literal: As before, the sequence of steps was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The sequence was carried out as before and completed.

sentences.zh: 三鼓舉赤旗，變銳陣，諸軍相屬，魚貫斜列，前利後張，為沖敵之形。

translations.literal: At the third drum the red flag was raised; changing to a sharp formation, the various armies linked in succession, arrayed obliquely like fish passing in file, sharp in front and spread in back, forming the shape of charging the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the third drumbeat the red flag went up; the formation changed to a wedge array, with the armies linked in succession and slanted in fish-scale lines—tapered in front and broad in rear—as a formation for charging the enemy.

sentences.zh: 亦依前節 次訖。

translations.literal: Likewise, following the previous sequence of steps, it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: This too followed the earlier sequence through to completion.

sentences.zh: 王逵奏人馬教絕，取旨。

translations.literal: Wang Kui reported that the men and horses had finished the drill, and sought the emperor's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui reported that the drill was complete and sought the emperor's orders.

sentences.zh: 舉青旗，變放教直陣，收鼓訖，一金止。

translations.literal: The green flag was raised; the formation changed to the dismissed-drill straight array; the drums ceased; one metal gong stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The green flag was raised; the troops shifted into the straight-line formation for dismissing the drill; the drums fell silent; and a single gong stroke signaled the halt.

sentences.zh: 重鼓三，馬軍下馬，步人齪落旗槍，皆應規矩。

translations.literal: Three heavy drumbeats; the horse army dismounted; the infantry snapped down flags and spears; all responded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Three heavy drumbeats sounded; the cavalry dismounted; the infantry lowered their flags and spears in unison; and all moved according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，犒賞倍之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and doubled the rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor doubled the soldiers' rewards.

sentences.zh: 士卒歡呼謝恩如儀。

translations.literal: The soldiers shouted in joy and thanked him for his grace according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cheered and thanked him for his grace according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 鳴 角聲簇隊訖，放教拽隊。

translations.literal: Horns were sounded; the formations clustered and were completed; the drill was dismissed and the companies were led away.
translations.idiomatic: Horns sounded; the units massed into formation; and the drill ended with the companies marching off.

sentences.zh: 步人分東西引拽，馬軍交頭於禦台下，隨隊呈試驍銳大刀武藝，繼而進呈車炮、火炮、煙槍。

translations.literal: The infantry divided east and west to lead the companies away; the horse army crossed paths below the imperial terrace; each company in turn displayed fierce great-blade martial skills; then they presented in succession wheeled cannon, fire cannon, and smoke guns.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry split east and west to lead the columns away; the cavalry crossed below the imperial terrace; each unit in turn demonstrated great-blade combat skills; and then wheeled guns, fire lances, and smoke guns were presented.

sentences.zh: 及赭山打圍射生，馬步軍統制官蕭鷓巴以所獲 獐鹿等就禦台下進獻，人馬拽絕。

translations.literal: And at Zhe Mountain's encircling hunt for game, the horse-and-foot army commander Xiao Zheba brought the roebuck, deer, and other game he had taken to present below the imperial terrace; the men and horses had finished the parade drill.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhe Mountain encirclement hunt, horse-and-foot army commander Xiao Zheba presented the roebuck, deer, and other quarry he had taken below the imperial terrace; the men and horses finished their parade drill.

sentences.zh: 皇帝復禦常服，乘馬至車子院，宣喚殿前司撥發官馬定遠、侯彥昌各賜馬一匹，彥昌仍自準備將特升副將。

translations.literal: The emperor again wore ordinary robes, mounted a horse, and went to the Chariot Court; he summoned the Palace Front Bureau dispatch officers Ma Dingyuan and Hou Yanchang and granted each a horse; Yanchang was also specially promoted from prepared general to deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed back to ordinary dress, rode to the Chariot Court, and summoned the Palace Front Bureau dispatch officers Ma Dingyuan and Hou Yanchang, granting each a horse; Yanchang was also promoted from prepared general to deputy general.

sentences.zh: 進禦酒，上謂王逵 曰：“今日教閱，進止分合，軍律整肅，皆卿之力也。

translations.literal: Imperial wine was presented; the emperor said to Wang Kui: "Today's drill review—the advances, halts, divisions, and reunions, and the army's strict discipline—are all owing to your effort.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial wine was brought forward, and the emperor said to Wang Kui, "Today's drill review—the timing of advances and halts, the splitting and reuniting of units, the army's discipline—all of this is your doing.

sentences.zh: ”逵奏：“陛下神武，四海共知。

translations.literal: " Kui reported: "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess is known throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: " Kui replied, "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 六師軍容，孰敢不肅！

translations.literal: Among the six armies' military bearing, who would dare not be disciplined!
translations.idiomatic: With the bearing of the imperial armies, who would dare be lax!

sentences.zh: ”時賜酒俱以十分，逵奏以軍馬事不敢飲，帝曰：“ 少飲之。

translations.literal: " At that time the wine granted was all in full measure; Kui reported that because of horse-and-army affairs he dared not drink; the emperor said: "Drink a little.
translations.idiomatic: " The wine granted was full measure for all; Kui said that with army and horse duties he dared not drink; the emperor said, "Take a little.

sentences.zh: ”親減大半。

translations.literal: " He personally reduced most of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor personally reduced most of the portion.

sentences.zh: 飲畢，謝恩退。

translations.literal: When the drinking was finished, he thanked him for the grace and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he had drunk, he thanked the emperor and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又宣問主管侍衛馬軍司李舜舉：“今日按閱之兵，比向時所用之師何如？

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned and questioned Supervisor of the Imperial Guard Horse Bureau Li Shunju: "Today's reviewed troops—how do they compare with the armies used in former times?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Li Shunju, supervisor of the Imperial Guard Horse Bureau, and asked, "How do today's reviewed troops compare with the armies of former times?

sentences.zh: ”舜舉奏曰：“今日所治之兵，皆陛下平時躬親訓 練，撫以深恩，賜之重賞，忠勇百倍，非昔日可比。

translations.literal: " Shunju reported: "Today's trained troops are all ones Your Majesty personally drilled in ordinary times, comforted with deep favor, and granted heavy rewards; their loyalty and courage are a hundredfold and cannot be compared with former days.
translations.idiomatic: " Shunju replied, "The troops reviewed today have all been personally trained by Your Majesty in peacetime, treated with deep kindness, and given generous rewards; their loyalty and courage are a hundred times what they were—nothing like the armies of old.

sentences.zh: ”其儀：皇帝至祥曦殿，行門、禁衛等並戎服迎駕常起居。

translations.literal: " The procedure: When the emperor arrived at Xiangxi Hall, the gate guards, imperial guards, and the rest all in military dress received the imperial progress and performed the regular attendance greeting.
translations.idiomatic: " The prescribed ritual: when the emperor arrived at Xiangxi Hall, the gate guards and imperial guards—all in military dress—received him and performed the regular attendance greeting.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至，知閣門官以下並戎服常起居，訖。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, the Director of the Gate Bureau and those below all in military dress performed the regular attendance greeting; this was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, the Director of the Gate Bureau and officials below him, all in military dress, performed the regular attendance greeting; then it was finished.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘馬 出，從駕官從駕至候潮門外大教場禦幄殿下馬，入幄更衣訖，皇帝被金甲出幄，行門、禁衛等迎駕，奏萬福。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and rode out; officials accompanying the progress followed to the great drill ground outside Chaohao Gate, dismounted below the imperial tent platform, entered the tent and changed clothes; when finished the emperor donned golden armor and came out of the tent; the gate guards, imperial guards, and the rest received the imperial progress and reported "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode out with his attendants to the great drill ground outside Chaohao Gate, where they dismounted below the imperial tent; he entered the tent to change, then emerged in golden armor; the gate guards and imperial guards received him and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘馬至教場台下馬，升台入幄。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and rode to the drill ground terrace, dismounted, ascended the terrace, and entered the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode to the drill ground terrace, dismounted, mounted the platform, and entered the tent.

sentences.zh: 從駕官宰執、親 王、使相、正任知閣、禦帶、環衛官升台，於幄殿分東西相向立。

translations.literal: The chief councillors, imperial princes, envoys with ministerial rank, regular appointees of the Gate Bureau, imperial guards with sword girdles, and palace guard officers who accompanied the progress ascended the terrace and, at the tent hall, divided east and west to stand facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors, imperial princes, envoys of ministerial rank, regular Gate Bureau appointees, sword-girdled imperial guards, and palace guard officers who accompanied the emperor ascended the platform and stood facing one another on east and west sides of the tent hall.

sentences.zh: 管軍並令全裝衣甲帶禦器械執骨朵升台，於幄殿指南面西立，俟入內官喝排立。

translations.literal: The army commanders were all ordered to ascend the terrace in full armor with imperial weapons, holding maces; they stood west of the southern side of the tent hall, awaiting the inner-service official's shouted command to line up.
translations.idiomatic: The army commanders were ordered to mount the platform in full armor with imperial weapons and ceremonial maces; they stood on the west side of the south face of the tent hall, waiting for an inner-court attendant to call them into formation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出幄，行門、 禁衛等迎駕，奏萬福。

translations.literal: The emperor came out of the tent; the gate guards, imperial guards, and the rest received the imperial progress and reported "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged from the tent; the gate guards and imperial guards received him and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 皇帝出，閣門分引殿前馬步三司統制、統領官常起居訖。

translations.literal: When the emperor came out, the Gate Bureau separately led the Palace Front horse-and-foot three bureaus' commanders and leader-officers to perform the regular attendance greeting; this was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came out, the Gate Bureau ushered in the Palace Front horse-and-foot commanders and leader-officers from the three bureaus for the regular attendance greeting; then it was done.

sentences.zh: 次三司將佐以下，聽鼓聲常起居。

translations.literal: Next, the three bureaus' adjutants and those below heeded the drum signal and performed the regular attendance greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Next, adjutants and junior officers of the three bureaus performed the regular attendance greeting at the drum signal.

sentences.zh: 次殿帥執骨朵赴御坐前，奏教直陣。

translations.literal: Next the Palace Commander, holding a mace, went before the imperial seat and reported requesting instruction in the straight array.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Palace Commander, mace in hand, went before the imperial seat and requested permission to drill the straight-line formation.

sentences.zh: 俟教閱畢，再 赴御坐前奏教圓陣。

translations.literal: When the instructional review was finished, he again went before the imperial seat and reported requesting instruction in the round array.
translations.idiomatic: When that drill was finished, he again went before the imperial seat and requested permission to drill the circular formation.

sentences.zh: 俟教閱畢，再赴御坐前奏教銳陣。

translations.literal: When the instructional review was finished, he again went before the imperial seat and reported requesting instruction in the sharp array.
translations.idiomatic: When that drill was finished, he again went before the imperial seat and requested permission to drill the wedge formation.

sentences.zh: 俟教閱畢，再赴御坐前奏教閱畢，歸侍立。

translations.literal: When the instructional review was finished, he again went before the imperial seat and reported that the instructional review was complete, then returned to attend standing by.
translations.idiomatic: When that drill was finished, he again went before the imperial seat to announce the review complete, then returned to his station.

sentences.zh: 內侍傳旨與殿前太尉某，諸軍謝恩承旨訖，轉與撥發官引三司統 制、統領、將佐再拜謝恩訖，各歸本軍。

translations.literal: An inner attendant transmitted the imperial order to a certain Palace Front grand marshal; the armies thanked him for the grace and received the order; it was passed to the dispatch officer, who led the three bureaus' commanders, leaders, and adjutants to bow twice in thanks for the grace; each returned to his army.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant conveyed the imperial order to the Palace Front grand marshal; after the armies received the order and thanked the emperor, a dispatch officer led the three bureaus' commanders, leaders, and adjutants in a double bow of thanks; then each returned to his unit.

sentences.zh: 皇帝起，入幄更衣訖，皇帝出幄。

translations.literal: The emperor rose, entered the tent and changed clothes; when finished the emperor came out of the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose, entered the tent to change clothes, then came out again.

sentences.zh: 皇帝坐，舍人引宰執墪後立，俟進禦茶床。

translations.literal: The emperor sat; the usher led the chief councillors to kneel behind and stand, awaiting presentation of the imperial tea table.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat; ushers led the chief councillors to kneel and stand behind him, awaiting the imperial tea service.

sentences.zh: 舍人贊就坐，宰執躬身應喏訖，直身立，就 坐。

translations.literal: The usher proclaimed "Be seated"; the chief councillors bowed their bodies and responded "Yes"; when finished they stood erect and took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced that they might sit; the chief councillors bowed and answered "Yes"; then they straightened and took their seats.

sentences.zh: 進第一盞酒，起立墪後，俟皇帝飲酒訖，舍人贊就坐，躬身應喏訖，直身立。

translations.literal: When the first cup of wine was presented, they rose and knelt behind; when the emperor had finished drinking, the usher proclaimed "Be seated"; they bowed their bodies and responded "Yes"; when finished they stood erect.
translations.idiomatic: At the first round of wine they rose and knelt behind; when the emperor had finished drinking, the usher announced they might sit; they bowed, answered "Yes," and stood upright.

sentences.zh: 俟宰執酒至，接盞飲酒訖，盞付殿侍。

translations.literal: When the chief councillors' wine arrived, they received the cups, finished drinking, and handed the cups to the palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When their own wine was served, they took their cups, drank, and handed the cups to palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 次舍人贊食，並如儀。

translations.literal: Next the usher proclaimed the food; all was according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Next the usher announced the food service; everything proceeded according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 至第四盞，傳旨宣勸 訖，禦藥傳旨不拜，舍人承旨贊不拜，贊就坐。

translations.literal: At the fourth cup, the imperial order to encourage drinking was transmitted; the imperial pharmacy transmitted the order of no bowing; the usher received the order and proclaimed no bowing; he proclaimed "Be seated."
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth round the emperor's order to urge them to drink was conveyed; through the imperial pharmacy came the order that they need not bow; the usher received it and announced that no bow was required, then announced they might sit.

sentences.zh: 第五盞宣勸如第四盞儀。

translations.literal: The fifth cup's encouragement to drink followed the ritual of the fourth cup.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth round of urging to drink followed the same ritual as the fourth.

sentences.zh: 酒食畢，舉禦茶床。

translations.literal: When the wine and food were finished, the imperial tea table was raised.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine and food were finished, the imperial tea service was brought forward.

sentences.zh: 舍人分引宰執於幄殿重行立，禦藥傳旨不拜，舍人承旨訖，揖宰執躬身 贊不拜，各祗候直身立，降踏道歸幕次。

translations.literal: The usher separately led the chief councillors to stand in double rows at the tent hall; the imperial pharmacy transmitted the order of no bowing; when the usher had received the order, he bowed to the chief councillors and with bowed body proclaimed no bowing; each attended respectfully standing erect, descended the stairway, and returned to their tent stations.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers led the chief councillors to stand in double rows at the tent hall; through the imperial pharmacy came the order that they need not bow; the usher received it, bowed to the councillors, and announced that no bow was required; each stood at attention, descended the steps, and returned to their tent stations.

sentences.zh: 皇帝起，乘馬至車子院下馬。

translations.literal: The emperor rose, mounted a horse, and went to the Chariot Court, where he dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose, rode to the Chariot Court, and dismounted.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出幄，至車子院門樓上，出賜親王酒，再拜謝訖；

translations.literal: The emperor came out of the tent and went to the upper story of the Chariot Court gate tower; he granted wine to the imperial princes; they bowed twice in thanks; when finished;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged from the tent and went to the upper story of the Chariot Court gate tower; he granted wine to the imperial princes, who bowed twice in thanks;

sentences.zh: 次賜使相、正任並管軍，知閣、禦帶、 環衛官酒訖；

translations.literal: Next he granted wine to envoys of ministerial rank, regular appointees, and army commanders, Gate Bureau officials, imperial guards with sword girdles, and palace guard officers; when finished;
translations.idiomatic: Next he granted wine to ministerial envoys, regular appointees, and army commanders, Gate Bureau officials, sword-girdled imperial guards, and palace guard officers;

sentences.zh: 逐班再拜謝，訖，依舊相向立。

translations.literal: Each rank in turn bowed twice in thanks; when finished, they again stood facing one another as before.
translations.idiomatic: Each group bowed twice in thanks in turn; when finished, they again stood facing one another as before.

sentences.zh: 次親王執盞進皇帝酒，皇帝飲酒訖，一班再拜謝，訖；

translations.literal: Next the imperial princes held cups and presented wine to the emperor; when the emperor had finished drinking, the rank bowed twice in thanks; when finished;
translations.idiomatic: Next the imperial princes brought cups forward and offered wine to the emperor; when he had drunk, the group bowed twice in thanks;

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝觀畢，起，降車子院門樓歸幄。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished viewing, he rose, descended from the Chariot Court gate tower, and returned to the tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had finished viewing, he rose, came down from the Chariot Court gate tower, and returned to the tent.

sentences.zh: 親王以下退，皇帝乘馬出 車子院門，行門、禁衛等迎駕，奏萬福。

translations.literal: The imperial princes and those below withdrew; the emperor mounted and rode out through the Chariot Court gate; the gate guards, imperial guards, and the rest received the imperial progress and reported "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial princes and those below withdrew; the emperor rode out through the Chariot Court gate; the gate guards and imperial guards received him and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘馬至候潮門外大教場，應從駕官並戎服乘馬從駕回。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and rode to the great drill ground outside Chaohao Gate; all officials who should accompany the progress also in military dress mounted and followed the progress back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode to the great drill ground outside Chaohao Gate; all officials who should accompany him also in military dress mounted and rode back with him.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘馬入和寧門，至祥曦殿上下馬還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and rode in through Hening Gate, and at Xiangxi Hall dismounted and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode in through Hening Gate and, at Xiangxi Hall, dismounted and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 餘仿此。

translations.literal: The remainder follows this model.
translations.idiomatic: The rest follows this procedure.

sentences.zh: 淳熙四年十二月，大閱于茅灘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Chunxi, a grand review was held at Maotan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Chunxi 4, a grand military review was held at Maotan.

sentences.zh: 十年十一月，大閱於龍山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the tenth year, a grand review was held at Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 10, a grand review was held at Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，大閱于城南大教場。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year, a grand review was held at the great drill ground south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 16, a grand review was held at the great drill ground south of the city.

sentences.zh: 並如上儀。

translations.literal: All followed the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: All followed the ritual described above.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年十月，以在諒闇，令宰執於大教場教閱。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Qingyuan, because the emperor was in mourning seclusion, he ordered the chief councillors to conduct the instructional review at the great drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qingyuan 1, because the emperor was in mourning seclusion, he had the chief councillors conduct the drill review at the great drill ground.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，大閱于茅灘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, a grand review was held at Maotan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 2, a grand review was held at Maotan.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年十二月，幸候潮門外教場大閱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jiatai, the emperor visited the drill ground outside Chaohao Gate for a grand review.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Jiatai 2, the emperor visited the drill ground outside Chaohao Gate for a grand review.

sentences.zh: 端平二年四月大閱，以時暑，不及行。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Duanping a grand review was planned, but because of the seasonal heat it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: A grand review was planned for the fourth month of Duanping 2, but the summer heat prevented it from being held.

sentences.zh: 受降獻俘。

translations.literal: Accepting surrender and presenting captives.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting Surrender and Presenting Captives.

sentences.zh: 太祖平蜀，孟昶降，詔有司約前代儀制為受降禮。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Shu, Meng Chang surrendered; an edict ordered the responsible offices to draw on former dynasties' ritual institutions to establish the rite of accepting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu pacified Shu and Meng Chang surrendered, he ordered officials to adapt earlier dynasties' ceremonial protocols for a surrender rite.

sentences.zh: 昶至前一日，設御坐仗衛於崇元殿，如元會儀。

translations.literal: The day before Chang arrived, the imperial throne and guard of honor were set up in Chongyuan Hall, as in the New Year's assembly ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The day before Chang's arrival, the imperial throne and guard of honor were set up in Chongyuan Hall according to the New Year's assembly rite.

sentences.zh: 至日，大陳馬步諸軍於天街左右，設昶及其官屬素案 席褥於明德門外，表案於橫街北。

translations.literal: On the day of arrival, horse and foot armies were deployed in grand array on left and right of the Heavenly Street; plain mats and cushions for Chang and his officials were set up outside Mingde Gate, and the memorial table at the north of Cross Street.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, cavalry and infantry were marshaled along both sides of the Heavenly Street; plain mats and cushions for Chang and his entourage were placed outside Mingde Gate, with a table for the memorial on the north side of Cross Street.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引昶及其官屬素服紗帽北向序立。

translations.literal: The interpreter attendant led Chang and his officials in plain dress and gauze caps to stand in order facing north.
translations.idiomatic: An interpreter attendant led Chang and his officials, dressed in plain robes and gauze caps, to stand in order facing north.

sentences.zh: 昶跪奉表授閣門使，復位待命。

translations.literal: Chang knelt, presented the memorial, and handed it to the gate commissioner; he returned to his place and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chang knelt, offered the memorial to the gate commissioner, returned to his place, and awaited orders.

sentences.zh: 表至御前，侍臣讀訖，閣門使承旨出。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the imperial presence, attendant ministers read it through; the gate commissioner received the order and went out.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, attendant ministers read it aloud; the gate commissioner received the imperial order and went out.

sentences.zh: 昶等俯伏。

translations.literal: Chang and the others prostrated themselves face down.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and his party prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 通事 舍人掖昶起，官屬亦起，宣制釋罪，昶等再拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The interpreter attendant helped Chang rise; the officials also rose; the imperial pronouncement released them from guilt; Chang and the others bowed twice and shouted "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: An interpreter attendant helped Chang to his feet, and his officials rose as well; an imperial pronouncement absolved them of guilt; Chang and his party bowed twice and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 衣庫使導所賜襲衣、冠帶陳於前，昶等又再拜跪受，改服乘馬，至升龍門下馬，官屬至啟運門下馬，就次。

translations.literal: The wardrobe commissioner led forward the granted court robes, caps, and belts and displayed them; Chang and the others again bowed twice, knelt, and received them; they changed dress, mounted horses, and at Shenglong Gate dismounted; the officials dismounted at Qiyun Gate and took their stations.
translations.idiomatic: The wardrobe commissioner presented the granted court robes, caps, and belts; Chang and his party bowed twice, knelt, and received them; they changed clothes, mounted horses, and dismounted at Shenglong Gate; the officials dismounted at Qiyun Gate and took their assigned places.

sentences.zh: 帝 常服升坐，百官先入起居，班立。

translations.literal: The emperor in ordinary dress ascended and took his seat; the hundred officials first entered, performed attendance greetings, and stood in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in ordinary dress, took the throne; officials entered first, paid their respects, and stood in formation.

sentences.zh: 閣門使引昶等入，舞蹈拜謝。

translations.literal: The gate commissioner led Chang and the others in; they performed the dance bow of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The gate commissioner ushered in Chang and his party; they performed the ceremonial bow of thanks.

sentences.zh: 召昶升殿，閣門使引自東階升，宣撫使承旨安撫之。

translations.literal: Chang was summoned to ascend the hall; the gate commissioner led him up by the eastern stairs; the pacification commissioner received the order and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was summoned to ascend the hall; the gate commissioner led him up the eastern steps; a pacification commissioner received the imperial order and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 昶至御坐前，躬承問訖，還位，與官屬舞蹈出。

translations.literal: Chang reached before the imperial seat, bowed and received inquiries; when finished he returned to his place and, with his officials, performed the dance bow and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang came before the throne, bowed and answered the emperor's inquiries; then he returned to his place and left with his officials after the ceremonial bow.

sentences.zh: 中書率百官稱賀，遂宴近臣及昶於大明殿。

translations.literal: The Secretariat led the hundred officials in offering congratulations; then a feast was held for close ministers and Chang in Daming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat led the officials in offering congratulations; then the emperor hosted a banquet for close ministers and Chang in Daming Hall.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，劉鋹就擒，詔有司撰獻俘禮。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, Liu Chang was captured; an edict ordered the responsible offices to draft the rite of presenting captives.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingnan was pacified and Liu Chang was captured, the emperor ordered officials to draft the captive-presentation rite.

sentences.zh: 鋹至，上御明德門，列仗衛，諸軍、百官常服班樓前。

translations.literal: When Chang arrived, the emperor took position at Mingde Gate; guards of honor were arrayed; the armies and hundred officials in ordinary dress ranked before the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang arrived, the emperor took his place at Mingde Gate; guards of honor were drawn up; the armies and officials in ordinary dress stood in ranks before the gate tower.

sentences.zh: 別設獻俘位於 東西街之南，北向；

translations.literal: A captive-presentation place was set separately south of the east-west streets, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: A separate captive-presentation station was set up south of the east-west cross streets, facing north;

sentences.zh: 其將校位於獻俘位前，北上西向。

translations.literal: His generals and officers took positions before the captive-presentation place, on the north side facing west.
translations.idiomatic: His generals and officers took positions before the captive-presentation station, on the north side facing west.

sentences.zh: 有司率武士系鋹等白練，露布前引。

translations.literal: The responsible office led warriors who bound Chang and the others with white silk; a battle report went ahead to lead the way.
translations.idiomatic: Officials led warriors who bound Liu Chang and the others with white cords; a victory report was carried ahead to lead the procession.

sentences.zh: 至太廟西南門，鋹等並下馬，入南神門，北向西上立，監將校官次南立。

translations.literal: Reaching the southwest gate of the Grand Temple, Chang and the others all dismounted, entered the South Spirit Gate, stood facing west on the north side of the ascent; supervising generals and officers stood in order on the south.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Grand Temple's southwest gate, Liu Chang and the others all dismounted, entered the South Spirit Gate, and stood facing west on the northern rise; supervising generals and officers stood in order to the south.

sentences.zh: 俟告禮畢，於西南門出，乘馬押至太社，如上儀。

translations.literal: When the announcement rite was finished, they went out through the southwest gate, mounted horses, and were escorted to the Grand Earth Altar, following the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: When the announcement rite was finished, they left through the southwest gate, mounted, and were escorted to the Grand Earth Altar according to the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 乃押至樓南禦路之西，下馬立俟。

translations.literal: Then they were escorted to the west of the imperial road south of the gate tower, dismounted, and stood awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: They were then escorted to the west side of the imperial road south of the gate tower, where they dismounted and stood awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 獻俘將校，戎服帶刀。

translations.literal: The generals and officers presenting the captives wore military dress and carried swords.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and officers presenting the captives wore military dress with swords at their belts.

sentences.zh: 攝侍中版奏中嚴，百官班定；

translations.literal: The acting attendant-in-chief reported by wooden tablet that the middle watch was strict; the hundred officials' ranks were set;
translations.idiomatic: The acting attendant-in-chief announced by wooden tablet that the middle watch was strict; the officials' ranks were set;

sentences.zh: 版奏外辦，帝常服御坐。

translations.literal: The wooden tablet reported that the outer preparations were complete; the emperor in ordinary dress took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden-tablet announcement reported that outer preparations were complete; the emperor, in ordinary dress, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 百 官舞蹈起居畢，通事舍人引鋹就獻俘位，將校等詣樓前舞蹈訖，次引露布案詣樓前北向，宣付中書、門下，如宣制儀。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials had finished the dance bow and attendance greeting, the interpreter attendant led Chang to the captive-presentation place; the generals and officers went before the gate tower and finished the dance bow; next the battle-report table was led before the gate tower facing north; the pronouncement was delivered to the Secretariat and Chancellery, as in the pronouncement ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had performed the ceremonial greeting, an interpreter attendant led Liu Chang to the captive-presentation station; his generals and officers performed the ceremonial bow before the gate tower; then the victory-report table was brought before the tower facing north and the pronouncement was delivered to the Secretariat and Chancellery according to the pronouncement protocol.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人跪受露布，轉授中書，門下轉授攝兵 部尚書。

translations.literal: The interpreter attendant knelt, received the battle report, and passed it to the Secretariat; the Chancellery passed it to the acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreter attendant knelt, received the victory report, and passed it to the Secretariat; the Chancellery forwarded it to the acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 次攝刑部尚書詣樓前跪奏以所獻俘付有司。

translations.literal: Next the acting Minister of Punishments went before the gate tower, knelt, and reported that the presented captives were handed over to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Next the acting Minister of Punishments went before the gate tower, knelt, and reported that the captives were handed over to the responsible authorities.

sentences.zh: 上召鋹詰責，鋹伏地待罪。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Chang and interrogated and rebuked him; Chang lay face down awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Liu Chang and rebuked him; Liu Chang prostrated himself awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔誅其臣龔澄樞等，特釋鋹縛與其弟保興等罪，仍賜襲衣、冠帶、靴笏、器幣、鞍 馬，各服其服列謝樓下。

translations.literal: An edict executed his ministers Gong Chenshu and others; Chang's bonds and those of his brother Baoxing and the rest were specially released from guilt; court robes, caps, belts, boots, tablets, vessels, coins, saddles, and horses were still granted; each put on his robes and lined up below the tower to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the execution of his ministers Gong Chenshu and others; Liu Chang's bonds and those of his brother Baoxing and the rest were specially remitted; they were granted court robes, caps, belts, boots, tablets, gifts, saddles, and horses; and each donned his new garments and lined up below the tower to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 百官稱賀畢，放仗如儀。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials had finished offering congratulations, the guard of honor was dismissed according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had offered congratulations, the guard of honor was dismissed according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 南唐平，帝御明德門，露布引李煜及其子弟官屬素服待罪。

translations.literal: When Southern Tang was pacified, the emperor took position at Mingde Gate; a battle report led Li Yu and his sons, younger brothers, and officials in plain dress to await judgment for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Tang was pacified, the emperor took his place at Mingde Gate; a victory report led Li Yu, his sons and brothers, and his officials—dressed in plain robes—to await judgment for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 初，有司請如獻劉鋹。

translations.literal: At first, the responsible offices requested following the presentation of Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At first, officials asked to follow the Liu Chang captive-presentation procedure.

sentences.zh: 帝以煜奉正朔，非若鋹拒命，寢露布弗宣，遣閣門使承制釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yu had accepted the imperial calendar and was not like Chang in defying orders, shelved the victory report and did not proclaim it, and sent a gate commissioner to receive the imperial order and release him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Li Yu had acknowledged Song suzerainty, unlike Liu Chang, who had defied imperial orders; he therefore suppressed the victory report and sent a gate commissioner to receive the imperial order and absolve him.

sentences.zh: 太宗征太原，劉繼元降，帝幸城北，陳兵衛，張樂，宴從臣於城台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan and Liu Jiyuan surrendered, the emperor visited the north of the city, deployed guards of honor, set out music, and feasted his attending ministers on the city terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Taiyuan and Liu Jiyuan surrendered, the emperor visited the north side of the city, drew up guards of honor, set out music, and hosted a banquet for his attending ministers on the city terrace.

sentences.zh: 繼元帥官屬素服台下。

translations.literal: Jiyuan led his officials in plain dress below the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiyuan led his officials, dressed in plain robes, to stand below the terrace.

sentences.zh: 遣閣門使宣制釋罪，召繼元親勞之。

translations.literal: He sent a gate commissioner to proclaim the imperial order releasing them from guilt, and summoned Jiyuan to comfort him in person.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a gate commissioner to proclaim an imperial order absolving them of guilt, then summoned Liu Jiyuan and personally reassured him.

sentences.zh: 從臣詣行宮稱賀。

translations.literal: The attending ministers went to the traveling palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The attending ministers went to the traveling palace to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 時以在軍中，故 不備禮。

translations.literal: Because they were then in the army, the full ritual was not observed.
translations.idiomatic: Because they were in camp at the time, the full ceremony was not performed.

sentences.zh: 繼元至京師，詔告獻太廟。

translations.literal: When Jiyuan reached the capital, an edict ordered announcement and presentation at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan reached the capital, an edict ordered the temple announcement and presentation rite at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 前一日，所司陳設如常告廟儀。

translations.literal: On the day before, the responsible office set out arrangements according to the usual temple-announcement ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the responsible office arranged the setting according to the usual temple-announcement protocol.

sentences.zh: 告日黎明，博士引太尉就位，通事舍人引繼元西階下東向立，其官屬重行立。

translations.literal: At dawn on the announcement day, the scholar of ceremonies led the grand marshal to his place; the interpreter attendant led Jiyuan to stand facing east below the western stairs, and his officials stood in double ranks.
