translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the announcement day, a scholar of ceremonies led the grand marshal to his place; an interpreter attendant led Liu Jiyuan to stand facing east below the western stairs, while his officials stood in double ranks.

sentences.zh: 贊者贊太尉再拜 訖，博士引就盥爵如常儀，詣東階解劍脫舄，升第一室進奠，再拜，太祝跪讀祝文訖，又再拜。

translations.literal: The proclaimer directed the grand marshal to bow twice; when finished, the scholar led him to the hand-washing and libation station according to usual ritual, to the eastern stairs to remove sword and shoes, ascended the first chamber to present offerings, bowed twice; the chief temple invocator knelt, read the prayer text through, and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: A proclaimer directed the grand marshal to bow twice; when that was done, the scholar of ceremonies led him to wash hands and receive the libation cup according to usual rite, then to the eastern stairs to remove his sword and shoes. He ascended the first chamber to present offerings and bow twice; the chief temple invocator knelt, read the prayer text aloud, and he bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引繼元及官屬詣室前西階下北向立，舍人贊云：“皇帝親 征，收復河東，偽主劉繼元及偽命官見。

translations.literal: The interpreter attendant led Jiyuan and his officials to stand facing north below the western stairs before the chamber; the usher proclaimed: "The emperor personally campaigned, recovered Hedong; the false ruler Liu Jiyuan and officials appointed by the false regime are present."
translations.idiomatic: An interpreter attendant led Liu Jiyuan and his officials to stand facing north below the western stairs before the chamber; an usher proclaimed, "The emperor personally took the field, recovered Hedong, and the false ruler Liu Jiyuan and the officials of his false regime are present."

sentences.zh: ”贊者曰再拜，拜訖退位。

translations.literal: " The proclaimer said "Bow twice"; when the bows were finished they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The proclaimer called for them to bow twice; when the bows were finished, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次至第二、第三、第四、第五室，皆如第一室。

translations.literal: Next they proceeded to the second, third, fourth, and fifth chambers, all as in the first chamber.
translations.idiomatic: They then proceeded to the second, third, fourth, and fifth chambers, each according to the same procedure as the first.

sentences.zh: 博士引太尉降階，佩劍納履復位，贊者曰再拜， 太尉與繼元等皆再拜，退。

translations.literal: The scholar led the grand marshal down the stairs, girded his sword, put on his shoes, and returned to his place; the proclaimer said "Bow twice"; the grand marshal and Jiyuan and the others all bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar of ceremonies led the grand marshal down the stairs, where he girded on his sword, put on his shoes, and returned to his place. The proclaimer called for another bow; the grand marshal, Liu Jiyuan, and the others all bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 焚祝版於齋坊。

translations.literal: The prayer tablets were burned at the abstinence lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer tablets were burned in the abstinence lodge.

sentences.zh: 繼元既命以官，故不稱俘焉。

translations.literal: Because Jiyuan had already been granted official appointment, he was not called a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Jiyuan had already been granted an official appointment, he was not styled a captive.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，西蕃王攏拶、邈川首領瞎征等降，詔具儀注。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, the Western Tibetan king Longzai, the Miaochuan chieftain Xiazheng, and others surrendered; an edict ordered full ritual specifications prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 2, the Western Tibetan king Longzai, the Miaochuan chieftain Xiazheng, and others surrendered; the court ordered full ceremonial regulations drawn up.

sentences.zh: 以受降日禦宣德門， 設諸班直、上四軍仗衛，諸軍素服陳列。

translations.literal: On the day of accepting surrender he took position at Xuande Gate, set out all guard shifts and the upper-four-army guard of honor, and all armies stood in formation in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the surrender-acceptance day the emperor took his place at Xuande Gate, arranged all guard shifts and the upper-four-army guard of honor, and the armies stood in formation dressed in plain robes.

sentences.zh: 降者各服蕃服以見，審問訖，有旨放罪，各等第賜首服袍帶。

translations.literal: Each of the surrendering parties wore tribal dress to be received; when inquiry was finished, an imperial rescript released them from guilt, and each was granted court robes, caps, and belts by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each surrendering party appeared in tribal dress; after inquiry, an imperial rescript absolved them of guilt, and each was granted court robes, caps, and belts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 百官稱賀，而再禦紫宸殿賜宴會。

translations.literal: The hundred officials offered congratulations, and he again took position at Zichen Hall and granted a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The officials offered congratulations, and the emperor then took his place again at Zichen Hall and hosted a banquet.

sentences.zh: 哲宗崩，樞密院留攏拶等西 京聽旨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong died, the Bureau of Military Affairs kept Longzai and the others at the Western Capital awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong died, the Bureau of Military Affairs kept Longzai and his party at the Western Capital awaiting instructions.

sentences.zh: 詔罷禦樓立仗，但引見於後殿。

translations.literal: An edict abolished taking position on the gate tower with guard drawn up, and only led them in audience at the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the ceremony of taking position on the gate tower with guards drawn up; they were received only in audience at the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 攏拶一班，契丹公主一班，夏國、回鶻公主次之，瞎征一班，邊廝波結並族屬次之。

translations.literal: Longzai one rank, Khitan princess one rank, Western Xia and Uyghur princesses next, Xiazheng one rank, Bian Sibo and kinsmen next.
translations.idiomatic: Longzai formed one rank, a Khitan princess another, Western Xia and Uyghur princesses came next, Xiazheng formed a rank, and Bian Sibo with his kinsmen followed.

sentences.zh: 應族屬首領各從其長，以次起居。

translations.literal: The corresponding tribal leaders each followed their chief and paid their respects in order.
translations.idiomatic: The corresponding tribal leaders each followed their own chief and paid their respects in turn.

sentences.zh: 僧尼 公主皆蕃服蕃拜。

translations.literal: Monks, nuns, and princesses all wore tribal dress and performed tribal obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Monks, nuns, and princesses all wore tribal dress and performed tribal obeisance.

sentences.zh: 並賜冠服，謝訖，賜酒饌橫門外。

translations.literal: All were granted caps and robes; when thanks were finished, food and wine were bestowed outside Heng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: All were granted caps and robes; after they had given thanks, food and wine were bestowed outside Heng Gate.

sentences.zh: 政和初，議禮局上《受降儀》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe, the Ritual Discussion Bureau submitted the "Rites for Accepting Surrender."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenghe reign, the Ritual Discussion Bureau submitted the Rites for Accepting Surrender.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輿升宣德門樓，降輿坐禦幄，百官與降王、蕃官各班樓下， 如大禮肆赦儀。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the imperial carriage up Xuande Gate tower, descended and sat in the imperial pavilion; the hundred officials, surrendering kings, and tribal officials took their ranks below the tower, as in the great general-amnesty ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode the imperial carriage up Xuande Gate tower, then descended and took his seat in the imperial pavilion; officials, surrendering kings, and tribal officials formed their ranks below the tower, as in the great general-amnesty ceremony.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門以紅絛袋班齊牌引升樓，樓上東上閣門官附內侍承旨索扇，扇合，帝即御坐，簾卷。

translations.literal: The east upper pavilion gate led them up the tower with red-cord rank-alignment tokens; the east upper pavilion gate officer on the tower relayed the order through an inner attendant to request the fans; the fans closed; the emperor then took the imperial seat; the curtain rolled up.
translations.idiomatic: The east upper pavilion gate led them up the tower with red-cord rank tokens; on the tower, an east upper pavilion gate officer relayed the order through an inner attendant to request the fans. When the fans closed, the emperor took the throne and the curtain was raised.

sentences.zh: 內侍又贊扇開，侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The inner attendant again proclaimed the fans open; the guards followed the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant again proclaimed the fans open, and the guards took their stations according to usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 諸班親從並裡圍降王人等 迎駕，自贊常起居。

translations.literal: All guard ranks and close attendants together encircled the surrendering kings and others to welcome the imperial progress, and themselves proclaimed the usual attendance greeting.
translations.idiomatic: All guard ranks and close attendants encircled the surrendering kings and their party to welcome the imperial progress and themselves performed the usual attendance greeting.

sentences.zh: 次舍人贊執儀將士常起居。

translations.literal: Next the usher proclaimed the ritual-holding soldiers' usual attendance greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Next an usher proclaimed the usual attendance greeting for the soldiers holding the ceremonial implements.

sentences.zh: 次管幹降王使臣並隨行舊蕃官常起居。

translations.literal: Next the supervising officials for the surrendering kings' envoys and the accompanying former tribal officials performed the usual attendance greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Next the supervising officials for the surrendering kings' envoys and the accompanying former tribal officials performed the usual attendance greeting.

sentences.zh: 次禮直官、舍人引百官橫行北向，贊者曰拜，在位官皆再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲， 又再拜。

translations.literal: Next the ritual officer and usher led the hundred officials transversely facing north; the proclaimer said "Bow"; all office-holders bowed twice with ceremonial dance, thrice cried "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Next a ritual officer and ushers led the officials to stand facing north in ranks; a proclaimer called for bows; all officeholders performed the ceremonial bow twice, cried "Long live the emperor" three times, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 班首奏聖躬萬福，又再拜退，百官各就東西位。

translations.literal: The head of the rank reported the sacred person ten thousand blessings; they bowed twice again and withdrew; the hundred officials each took east-west positions.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the rank reported that the emperor enjoyed ten thousand blessings; they bowed twice again and withdrew, and the officials each took their east-west positions.

sentences.zh: 舍人引降王服本國衣冠詣樓前北向，女婦少西立，僧又少西，尼立於後。

translations.literal: The usher led the surrendering kings in their native dress, robes, and caps to the north before the tower; women stood slightly west; monks stood further west; nuns stood behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers led the surrendering kings, dressed in the robes and caps of their own countries, to stand facing north before the tower; women stood slightly to the west, monks farther west, and nuns behind them.

sentences.zh: 入內省官詣御坐前承旨，傳樓上東 上閣門官承旨錄訖，以紅條袋降制樓下，東上閣門官承旨退。

translations.literal: Inner Secretariat officials went before the imperial seat to receive the order; they transmitted it to the east upper pavilion gate officer on the tower, who recorded it; a red-strip bag lowered the decree below the tower; the east upper pavilion gate officer received the order and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretariat officials went before the throne to receive the imperial order and transmitted it to the east upper pavilion gate officer on the tower, who recorded it. A red-strip bag lowered the decree to the foot of the tower; the east upper pavilion gate officer received the order and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 降王以下俯伏，東上閣門官至，令通事舍人掖之起，首領以下皆起，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The surrendering kings and those below prostrated themselves; when the east upper pavilion gate officer arrived, he ordered the interpreter attendant to help them rise; the chiefs and those below all rose and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendering kings and those below prostrated themselves. When the east upper pavilion gate officer arrived, he ordered an interpreter attendant to help them rise; the chiefs and those below all stood and bowed.

sentences.zh: 閣門宣有敕，降王以下再 拜，僧尼止躬呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The pavilion gate proclaimed there was an edict; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice; monks and nuns only bowed the body and cried "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion gate proclaimed that there was an edict; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice, while the monks and nuns only bowed and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 閣門錄敕旨付管幹官，降王等躬聽詰問。

translations.literal: The pavilion gate recorded the edict's intent and delivered it to the supervising officials; the surrendering kings and others bowed and listened to the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion gate recorded the edict and handed it to the supervising officials; the surrendering kings and their party bowed and listened to the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 如有復奏，閣門錄訖，仍以紅絛袋引升樓。

translations.literal: If there was a further memorial, the pavilion gate recorded it and again led them up the tower with the red-cord bag.
translations.idiomatic: If there was a further memorial, the pavilion gate recorded it and again led them up the tower with the red-cord bag.

sentences.zh: 如無復奏，入內省官詣御坐承旨，傳樓上閣門官稱有敕放 罪訖，舍人贊謝恩，降王以下再拜稱萬歲，復序立。

translations.literal: If there was no further memorial, Inner Secretariat officials went to the imperial seat to receive the order; they transmitted to the pavilion gate officer on the tower, who proclaimed that the edict releasing guilt was finished; the usher proclaimed thanks for grace; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice and cried "Ten thousand years," then returned to ordered standing.
translations.idiomatic: If there was no further memorial, Inner Secretariat officials went before the throne to receive the order and transmitted it to the pavilion gate officer on the tower, who proclaimed that the edict absolving them of guilt had been issued. An usher proclaimed thanks for the emperor's grace; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice, cried "Long live the emperor," and returned to their ordered ranks.

sentences.zh: 入內省官詣御坐承旨，傳樓上閣門官稱有敕各賜首服袍帶。

translations.literal: Inner Secretariat officials went to the imperial seat to receive the order and transmitted to the pavilion gate officer on the tower, who proclaimed that there was an edict granting each court robes, caps, and belts.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretariat officials went before the throne to receive the order and transmitted it to the pavilion gate officer on the tower, who proclaimed an edict granting each of them court robes, caps, and belts.

sentences.zh: 樓下閣門官承旨引所賜簷床陳於西，舍人宣曰有敕， 降王以下再拜鞠躬，舍人稱各賜某物，賜物畢，又再拜稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The pavilion gate officer below the tower received the order and led the granted folding screens to be displayed on the west; the usher proclaimed there was an edict; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice and bowed the body; the usher proclaimed each was granted certain items; when the gifts were finished, they again bowed twice and cried "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion gate officer below the tower received the order and had the granted gift screens set out on the west side. An usher proclaimed that there was an edict; the surrendering kings and those below bowed twice and bowed deeply. The usher announced each item granted, and when the gifts had been bestowed, they bowed twice again and cried, "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 若賜官、即贊謝再拜，並歸次易所賜服。

translations.literal: If offices were granted, then thanks were proclaimed and they bowed twice; all returned to their stations and changed into the granted garments.
translations.idiomatic: If offices were granted, thanks were proclaimed and they bowed twice; all then returned to their stations and changed into the garments they had been given.

sentences.zh: 舍人先引降王以下至授遙郡以上當樓前北向東上立，贊再 拜，稱萬歲，又再拜；

translations.literal: The usher first led the surrendering kings and those below up to those granted Remote Commandery rank and above to stand north before the tower facing east; proclaimed bow twice, cried "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again;
translations.idiomatic: Ushers first led the surrendering kings and those below, up to those who had been granted Remote Commandery rank and above, to stand north of the tower facing east; they were directed to bow twice, cry "Long live the emperor," and bow twice again;

sentences.zh: 次贊服冠帔婦女再拜。

translations.literal: Next proclaimed the women wearing caps and ceremonial robes to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: next the women wearing caps and ceremonial robes were directed to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 們尼別謝，引還。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns separately gave thanks and were led back.
translations.idiomatic: The monks and nuns gave thanks separately and were led back.

sentences.zh: 次贊樓上侍立官稱賀再拜，禮直官，舍人分引百官橫行北向立，贊拜訖，班首少前，俯伏跪，稱賀， 其詞中書隨事撰述，賀訖，復位。

translations.literal: Next proclaimed the standing attendants on the tower to offer congratulations and bow twice; the ritual officer and usher separately led the hundred officials transversely facing north; when the bow was finished, the head of the rank moved slightly forward, prostrated and knelt, offered congratulations—the text composed by the Secretariat according to the occasion; when congratulations were finished, he returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: Next the standing attendants on the tower were directed to offer congratulations and bow twice. A ritual officer and ushers separately led the officials to stand facing north in ranks; when the bow was finished, the head of the rank stepped slightly forward, prostrated himself, knelt, and offered congratulations in words composed by the Secretariat for the occasion; when congratulations were finished, he returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 在位者又再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲，又再拜。

translations.literal: Those in office again bowed twice with ceremonial dance, thrice cried "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Those in office again performed the ceremonial bow twice, cried "Long live the emperor" three times, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門官進詣樓前承旨，就班首宣曰有制，贊者曰拜，在位官皆再拜，宣答，其詞學士 院隨事撰述，又贊再拜，三稱萬歲，又再拜。

translations.literal: The east upper pavilion gate officer advanced to the front of the tower to receive the order, and at the head of the rank proclaimed there was a pronouncement; the proclaimer said "Bow"; all office-holders bowed twice; the response was proclaimed—the text composed by the Academy of Scholarly Worthies according to the occasion; again proclaimed bow twice, thrice cried "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: The east upper pavilion gate officer advanced to the front of the tower to receive the order and, before the head of the rank, proclaimed that there was an imperial pronouncement. A proclaimer called for bows; all officeholders bowed twice. The response was read aloud in words composed by the Academy of Scholarly Worthies for the occasion; they were again directed to bow twice, cry "Long live the emperor" three times, and bow twice again.

sentences.zh: 樓上樞密院前跪奏，稱某官臣某言，禮畢，內侍索扇，扇合簾垂，帝降坐。

translations.literal: Before the Bureau of Military Affairs on the tower knelt and memorialized, saying "A certain official, your subject X, reports"; when the rite was finished, the inner attendant requested the fans; the fans closed, the curtain lowered, and the emperor descended from the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Bureau of Military Affairs on the tower, an official knelt and memorialized, saying, "Your subject, official X, reports." When the rite was finished, an inner attendant requested the fans; the fans closed, the curtain fell, and the emperor left the throne.

sentences.zh: 內侍贊扇開，所司承旨放仗，樓下鞭鳴，百 官再拜退。

translations.literal: The inner attendant proclaimed the fans open; the responsible office received the order and dismissed the guard of honor; below the tower the whip sounded; the hundred officials bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant proclaimed the fans open; the responsible office received the order and dismissed the guard of honor; a whip sounded below the tower, and the officials bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年三月，四川宣撫副使安丙函逆臣吳曦首並違制創造法物、所受金國加封蜀王詔及金印來獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Kaixi, Sichuan pacification vice commissioner An Bing sent in a box the head of the rebel Wu Xi, together with ritual objects unlawfully manufactured, the edict by which the Jin had enfeoffed him King of Shu, and the Jin seal he had received.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaixi 3, Sichuan pacification vice commissioner An Bing sent in a box the head of the rebel Wu Xi, together with ritual objects he had unlawfully manufactured, the edict by which the Jin had enfeoffed him King of Shu, and the Jin seal he had received.

sentences.zh: 四月三日，禮部太常寺條具獻馘典故， 俟逆曦首函至日，臨安府差人防守，殿前司差甲士二百人同大理寺官監引赴都堂審驗。

translations.literal: On the third day of the fourth month, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices detailed the precedents for presenting severed heads; awaiting the day when Xi's head in its box arrived, Lin'an Prefecture dispatched men to guard it; the Palace Command dispatched two hundred armored soldiers together with chief justice officials to escort it to the main hall for examination.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the fourth month, the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set out the precedents for presenting enemy heads. When the box containing Wu Xi's head arrived, Lin'an Prefecture dispatched guards, and the Palace Command sent two hundred armored soldiers together with chief justice officials to escort it to the main hall for examination.

sentences.zh: 奏獻太廟、別廟差近上宗室南班，奏獻太社、太稷差侍從官。

translations.literal: For reporting presentation at the Grand Temple and separate temples, senior imperial clansmen from the southern rank were assigned; for reporting presentation at the Grand Earth and Grain altars, attendant ministers were assigned.
translations.idiomatic: For the presentation reports at the Grand Temple and the separate temples, senior imperial clansmen from the southern rank were assigned; for the reports at the Grand Earth and Grain altars, attendant ministers were assigned.

sentences.zh: 各前一日赴祠所 致齋，至日行奏獻之禮，大理寺、殿前司計會行禮時刻，監引首函設置以俟。

translations.literal: Each fasted one day before at the sacrificial site; on the day they performed the presentation rite; the chief justice and Palace Command coordinated the timing of the rite, escorted the head box, and set it in place awaiting the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Each spent the day before in ritual abstinence at the sacrificial site; on the appointed day they performed the presentation rite. The chief justice and the Palace Command coordinated the timing, escorted the box containing the head, and set it in place to await the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 奏獻禮畢，梟於市三日，付大理寺藏於庫。

translations.literal: When the presentation rite was finished, it was exposed at the market for three days, then handed to the chief justice for storage in the vault.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation rite was finished, the head was exposed at the market for three days, then handed over to the chief justice for storage in the vault.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，金亡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping, the Jin perished.
translations.idiomatic: In Duanping 1, the Jin dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 四月，京湖制置司以完顏守緒函骨來上，差官奏告宗廟社稷如儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Jinghu commissioner sent Wanyan Shouxu's boxed bones upward; officials were dispatched to announce at the ancestral temple and altars according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the Jinghu commissioner sent up a box containing the bones of Wanyan Shouxu; officials were dispatched to announce the event at the ancestral temple and the altars of state according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 田獵。

translations.literal: Field hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Field Hunting.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年，始校獵於近郊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong under Taizu, field-hunt reviews were first conducted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2, Emperor Taizu first conducted regulated field hunts in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 先出禁軍為圍場，五坊以鷙禽細犬從。

translations.literal: First the forbidden army was sent out to form the enclosure; the Five Workshops followed with fierce birds of prey and fine hounds.
translations.idiomatic: The forbidden army was first sent out to form the hunting enclosure, and the Five Workshops followed with fierce birds of prey and fine hounds.

sentences.zh: 帝親射走兔三，從官貢馬稱賀。

translations.literal: The emperor personally shot three fleeing hares; the attending officials presented horses in tribute and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally shot three fleeing hares, and the attending officials presented horses in tribute and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其後多以秋冬或正月田於四郊，從官或賜窄袍暖靴，親王以下射中者賜以馬。

translations.literal: Thereafter hunts were mostly conducted in autumn and winter or in the first month in the four suburbs; attending officials were sometimes granted narrow-sleeved robes and warm boots; imperial princes and those below who hit their targets were granted horses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter hunts were mostly held in autumn and winter or in the first month in the four suburbs; attending officials were sometimes granted narrow-sleeved robes and warm boots, and imperial princes and others who scored hits were given horses.

sentences.zh: 太宗將北征，因閱武獵近郊，以多盜獵狐兔者，命禁之。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign north, he conducted a martial review hunt in the near suburbs; because many thieves hunted foxes and hares, he ordered it forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was about to march north, he conducted a martial review hunt in the near suburbs; because many poachers were taking foxes and hares, he ordered the practice forbidden.

sentences.zh: 有衛士奪人獐，當死，帝曰：“若殺之，後世必謂我重獸而輕人。

translations.literal: A guard soldier seized someone's deer; the penalty was death; the emperor said: "If we kill him, later ages will surely say that I valued beasts and slighted men."
translations.idiomatic: A guard soldier seized another man's deer and was liable to death; the emperor said, "If we execute him, later ages will surely say that I valued beasts more than human lives."

sentences.zh: ”特貰其罪。

translations.literal: " He specially remitted his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He specially remitted the man's punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝常以臘日校獵，諭從臣 曰：“臘日出狩，以順時令，緩轡從禽，是非荒也。

translations.literal: The emperor often on La day conducted hunt reviews, telling his attending ministers: "On La day to go out hunting accords with the season; slack reins following game—this is not licentiousness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often conducted hunt reviews on La day and told his attending ministers, "To go out hunting on La day accords with the season, and to slacken the reins while following game is not idle dissipation."

sentences.zh: ”回幸講武台，張樂，賜群臣飲。

translations.literal: " Returning, he visited the Lecture-on-Arms Terrace, set out music, and granted the hundred ministers drink.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he visited the Lecture-on-Arms Terrace, set out music, and granted his ministers drink.

sentences.zh: 其後，獵西郊，親射走兔五。

translations.literal: Thereafter he hunted in the western suburbs and personally shot five fleeing hares.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he hunted in the western suburbs and personally shot five fleeing hares.

sentences.zh: 詔以古者蒐狩，以所獲之禽薦享宗廟，而其禮久 廢，今可復之。

translations.literal: An edict said that in antiquity the spring and autumn hunts used captured birds to offer at the ancestral temple, but that rite had long been abandoned; now it could be restored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that in antiquity the seasonal hunts used captured game to offer at the ancestral temple, but that rite had long fallen into disuse and could now be restored.

sentences.zh: 遂為定式。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was established as a fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was established as a fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 帝雅不好弋獵，詔除有司行禮外，罷近甸遊畋，五坊所畜鷹犬並放之，諸州不得以鷹來獻。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature disliked archery and hunting; an edict, except for the responsible offices performing rites, abolished pleasure hunting in the near districts; all hawks and hounds kept by the Five Workshops were released; all prefectures were forbidden to present hawks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature disliked archery and hunting; an edict abolished pleasure hunting in the near districts except when responsible offices were performing ritual duties, released all hawks and hounds kept by the Five Workshops, and forbade prefectures to present hawks as tribute.

sentences.zh: 已而定難軍節度使趙保忠獻鶻一，號“海東青 ”，詔還賜之。

translations.literal: Then Dingnan army commissioner Zhao Baozhong presented one hawk, called "Sea East Green"; an edict returned and bestowed it back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Dingnan army commissioner Zhao Baozhong presented a hawk called "Sea East Green"; an edict returned it to him as a gift.

sentences.zh: 臘日，但命諸王略畋近郊，而五坊之職廢矣。

translations.literal: On La day, only the imperial princes were ordered to hunt briefly in the near suburbs, and the function of the Five Workshops was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On La day only the imperial princes were ordered to hunt briefly in the near suburbs, and the functions of the Five Workshops were abolished.

sentences.zh: 真宗復詔教駿所養鷹鶻量留十餘，以備諸王從時展禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong again edicted that of the hawks and falcons raised by the hawk-training corps, a dozen or so should be kept, to supply the imperial princes when seasonally performing rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong again ordered that a dozen or so of the hawks and falcons raised by the hawk-training corps be kept on hand so that the imperial princes could perform seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 禁圍草地，許民耕牧。

translations.literal: Enclosed pasture lands were forbidden, and the people were permitted to farm and graze.
translations.idiomatic: Enclosed hunting pastures were opened, and common people were permitted to farm and graze there.

sentences.zh: 至仁宗時，言者言校獵之制所以順時令、訓戎事，請修此禮。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Renzong, memorialists said the field-hunt review system served to accord with the season and train martial affairs, and requested restoring this rite.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Renzong's reign, memorialists argued that the regulated field-hunt system served both to accord with the seasons and to train martial affairs, and they asked that the rite be restored.

sentences.zh: 於是詔樞密院奏定制度。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to memorialize and fix the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to draft and fix the regulations.

sentences.zh: 獵日五鼓，帝御內東門，賜從官酒三行，奏鈞容樂，幸瓊林苑門，賜從官 食。

translations.literal: On the hunt day at the fifth drumbeat, the emperor took position at the inner east gate, granted the attending officials three rounds of wine, performed Junrong music, visited Qionlin Garden gate, and granted the attending officials food.
translations.idiomatic: On hunt day, at the fifth drumbeat the emperor took his place at the inner east gate, granted his attending officials three rounds of wine, and had the Junrong ensemble perform. He then visited Qionlin Garden gate and granted his attendants food.

sentences.zh: 遂獵於楊村，宴於幄殿，奏教坊樂。

translations.literal: Then he hunted at Yang Village, banqueted at the pavilion hall, and performed Directorate music.
translations.idiomatic: He then hunted at Yang Village, banqueted in the pavilion hall, and had the Directorate of Music perform.

sentences.zh: 遣使以所獲馳薦太廟。

translations.literal: He dispatched an envoy to gallop-present the captures as offerings at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched an envoy to gallop-present the captured game as offerings at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 既而召父老臨問，賜以飲食茶絹，及五坊軍士銀絹有差。

translations.literal: Then he summoned elders to inquire face to face, bestowed food, drink, tea, and silk, and granted silver and silk to Five Workshops soldiers in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned local elders to question them in person and bestowed food, drink, tea, and silk upon them, while Five Workshops soldiers received silver and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 宰相賈昌朝等曰：“陛下暫幸近郊，順時田 獵，取鮮殺而登廟俎，所以昭孝德也；

translations.literal: Chief councillor Jia Changzhao and others said: "Your Majesty for a time visited the near suburbs, seasonally field-hunted, took fresh kill to ascend the temple altar—this displays filial virtue;"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Jia Changzhao and others said, "Your Majesty has for a time visited the near suburbs and hunted according to the season, taking fresh kill to the temple altar—this displays filial virtue;

sentences.zh: 即高原而閱軍實，所以講武事也；

translations.literal: ascended high ground to review military stores—this displays martial training;"
translations.idiomatic: you have ascended high ground to review military stores—this displays martial training;

sentences.zh: 問耆老而秩飫，所以養老也；

translations.literal: inquired of elders and honored them with feasting—this nourishes the aged;"
translations.idiomatic: you have questioned elders and honored them with ranked feasting—this nourishes the aged;

sentences.zh: 勞田夫而賜惠，所以勸農也。

translations.literal: labored for field workers and granted bounty—this encourages farming."
translations.idiomatic: you have consoled field workers and granted them bounty—this encourages farming.

sentences.zh: 乘輿一出，而四美皆具。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage once went out, and all four beauties were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In a single outing of the imperial carriage, all four virtues were fulfilled at once.

sentences.zh: 伏望宣 付史館。

translations.literal: Humbly hoping it be transmitted to the Historiography Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly ask that this be transmitted to the Historiography Bureau.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，復獵于城南東韓村。

translations.literal: The next year, he again hunted south of the city at East Han Village.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he hunted again south of the city at East Han Village.

sentences.zh: 自玉津園去輦乘馬，分騎士數千為左右翼，節以鼓旗。

translations.literal: From Yujin Garden he left the carriage and mounted horses; thousands of horsemen were divided into left and right wings, regulated with drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: From Yujin Garden he left his carriage and mounted; thousands of horsemen were divided into left and right wings and regulated with drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 合圍場徑十餘裡，部隊相應。

translations.literal: The combined enclosure was more than ten li in diameter; the units responded to one another.
translations.idiomatic: The combined hunting enclosure was more than ten li across, and the units coordinated with one another.

sentences.zh: 帝按轡中道，親挾弓矢，屢獲禽 焉。

translations.literal: The emperor held the reins on the middle path, personally wielded bow and arrows, and repeatedly captured game.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held the reins on the center path, personally wielded bow and arrows, and repeatedly brought down game.

sentences.zh: 是時，道傍居人或畜狐兔鳧雉驅場中。

translations.literal: At that time, residents along the road or those who kept foxes, hares, ducks, and pheasants drove them into the field.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, residents along the road, or people who kept foxes, hares, ducks, and pheasants, drove them into the enclosure.

sentences.zh: 帝謂田獵以訓武事，非專所獲也，悉縱之。

translations.literal: The emperor said field hunting trains martial affairs and is not solely for what is taken; he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that field hunting trains martial affairs and is not merely about what is taken, and he had them all released.

sentences.zh: 免圍內民田一歲租，仍召父老勞問。

translations.literal: One year's rent on farmland within the enclosure was remitted, and elders were summoned for consolatory inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted one year's rent on farmland within the enclosure and summoned local elders for consolatory visits.

sentences.zh: 其後以諫者多，罷獵近甸。

translations.literal: Thereafter, because memorialists were many, hunting in the near districts was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, because remonstrances were numerous, hunting in the near districts was abolished.

sentences.zh: 自是，終靖康 不復講。

translations.literal: From this time until the end of the Jingkang era, it was never again held.
translations.idiomatic: From that time until the fall of the Northern Song at Jingkang, hunting was never resumed.

sentences.zh: 打球，本軍中戲。

translations.literal: Striking the ball was originally a game within the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cuju ball-play was originally a pastime of the army.

sentences.zh: 太宗令有司詳定其儀。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the responsible offices to examine and fix its ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered officials to work out its ceremonial regulations in detail.

sentences.zh: 三月，會鞠大明殿。

translations.literal: In the third month, they assembled for cuju at the Hall of Great Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they gathered for cuju at the Hall of Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 有司除地，豎木東西為球門，高丈餘，首刻金龍，下施石蓮華坐，加以采繢。

translations.literal: The responsible offices cleared ground and erected posts east and west as ball goals more than one zhang high, carved with golden dragons at the top, set upon stone lotus seats below, and adorned with colored embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cleared a field and set up goalposts east and west, each more than one zhang tall, carved with golden dragons at the top, mounted on stone lotus pedestals below, and decorated with colored embroidery.

sentences.zh: 左 右分朋主之，以承旨二人守門，衛士二人持小紅旗唱籌，禦龍官錦繡衣持哥舒棒，周衛球場。

translations.literal: Left and right sides were divided into teams to preside; two Hanlin academicians guarded the goals, two guardsmen held small red flags and called out the tally, and Imperial Dragon officers in brocade robes held Geshu clubs and patrolled the ball ground.
translations.idiomatic: The players were divided into left and right teams; two Hanlin academicians guarded the goals, two guardsmen held small red flags and announced the score, and Imperial Dragon officers in brocade robes carrying Geshu clubs patrolled the field.

sentences.zh: 殿階下，東西建日月旗。

translations.literal: Below the hall steps, sun and moon banners were erected east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall steps, sun and moon banners were set up on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 教坊設龜茲部鼓樂於兩廊，鼓各五。

translations.literal: The Music Bureau set Kuche-section drums and music in both corridors, five drums in each.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Bureau placed Kuche-style drums and musicians in both corridors, five drums to each side.

sentences.zh: 又於東西 球門旗下各設鼓五。

translations.literal: Five drums were also set under the banners at each of the east and west ball goals.
translations.idiomatic: Five drums were also placed beneath the banners at each of the east and west goals.

sentences.zh: 閣門豫定分朋狀取裁。

translations.literal: The Gate Secretariat beforehand fixed the team rosters for approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Secretariat prepared the team rosters in advance for the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 親王、近臣、節度觀察防禦團練使、刺史、駙馬都尉、諸司使副使、供奉官、殿直悉預。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, close ministers, military commissioners, surveillance commissioners, defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, imperial sons-in-law, bureau commissioners and vice commissioners, palace attendants, and palace guards all participated.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, close ministers, military and civil commissioners of every rank, prefects, imperial sons-in-law, bureau commissioners and their deputies, palace attendants, and palace guards all took part.

sentences.zh: 其兩朋官，宗室、節度以下服異 色繡衣，左朋黃衤蘭；

translations.literal: Officials of the two teams—imperial clansmen and those below the rank of commissioner—wore embroidered garments of different colors; the left team wore yellow brocade;
translations.idiomatic: Officials on the two teams—members of the imperial clan and officers below commissioner rank—wore embroidered garments in contrasting colors; the left team wore yellow brocade;

sentences.zh: 右朋紫衤蘭打球供奉官左朋服紫繡，右朋服緋繡，烏皮靴，冠以華插腳折上巾。

translations.literal: the right team wore purple brocade; cuju palace attendants of the left team wore purple embroidery, those of the right team wore scarlet embroidery, black leather boots, and flower-decorated folded-up brim caps with inserted flaps.
translations.idiomatic: the right team wore purple brocade; cuju palace attendants on the left wore purple embroidery and those on the right scarlet embroidery, with black leather boots and ornate folded-up brim caps.

sentences.zh: 天廄院供馴習馬並鞍勒。

translations.literal: The Imperial Stud provided trained horses together with saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Stud supplied trained horses with saddles and bridles.

sentences.zh: 帝乘馬出，教坊大合《涼州曲》，諸 司使以下前導，從臣奉迎。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and rode out; the Music Bureau performed the full "Liangzhou Melody"; bureau commissioners and those below went ahead as guides, and attending ministers received him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted and rode out while the Music Bureau performed the full Liangzhou suite; bureau commissioners and lower officials went ahead as escorts, and attending ministers received him.

sentences.zh: 既禦殿，群臣謝，宣召以次上馬，馬皆結尾，分朋自兩廂入，序立於西廂。

translations.literal: Once he had reached the hall, the ministers gave thanks; they were summoned in order to mount; all the horses had braided tails; the teams entered from both side wings and lined up in order in the west wing.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the hall the ministers expressed their thanks; they were summoned in turn to mount horses with braided tails; the teams entered from both side wings and formed up in the west wing.

sentences.zh: 帝乘馬當庭西南駐。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted and halted his horse southwest of the courtyard center.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted and halted southwest of center court.

sentences.zh: 內侍發金合，出朱漆球擲殿前。

translations.literal: A eunuch opened a golden casket, took out a vermilion-lacquered ball, and cast it before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch opened a golden casket, produced a vermilion-lacquered ball, and tossed it out before the hall.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人 奏云：禦朋打東門。

translations.literal: The protocol officer memorialized, saying: "The imperial team will strike at the east goal."
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officer announced: "The imperial team will play toward the east goal."

sentences.zh: 帝擊球，教坊作樂奏鼓。

translations.literal: The emperor struck the ball; the Music Bureau performed music and beat drums.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck the ball as the Music Bureau played and the drums sounded.

sentences.zh: 球既度，颭旗、鳴鉦、止鼓。

translations.literal: Once the ball had passed through, banners were waved, bells sounded, and drums stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the ball passed through the goal, banners were waved, bells rang, and the drums fell silent.

sentences.zh: 帝回馬，從臣奉觴上壽，貢物以賀。

translations.literal: The emperor turned his horse; attending ministers presented cups to offer longevity and brought tribute objects in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned his horse; attending ministers offered cups in congratulation and presented tribute gifts.

sentences.zh: 賜酒，即列拜，飲畢上馬。

translations.literal: Wine was bestowed; they then lined up and bowed, and after drinking remounted.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was granted; they bowed in formation, and after drinking remounted their horses.

sentences.zh: 帝再擊之，始命諸王大臣 馳馬爭擊。

translations.literal: The emperor struck again, and only then ordered the princes and great ministers to gallop and compete in striking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck again, and only then ordered the princes and senior ministers to gallop and join the contest.

sentences.zh: 旗下擂鼓。

translations.literal: Drums were beaten under the banners.
translations.idiomatic: Drums were beaten beneath the goal banners.

sentences.zh: 將及門，逐廂急鼓。

translations.literal: As they neared the goal, drums were hurriedly beaten in each wing in turn.
translations.idiomatic: As players neared the goal, drums were beaten urgently in each wing in succession.

sentences.zh: 球度，殺鼓三通。

translations.literal: When the ball passed through, the drums were struck three times in decrescendo.
translations.idiomatic: When the ball went through the goal, the drums sounded three diminishing beats.

sentences.zh: 球門兩旁置繡旗二十四，而設虛架於殿東西階下。

translations.literal: Twenty-four embroidered banners were placed on both sides of the ball goals, and empty racks were set below the east and west steps of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four embroidered banners were placed beside the goals, and empty racks were set below the east and west hall steps.

sentences.zh: 每朋得籌，既插一旗架上以識之。

translations.literal: Whenever a team scored, a banner was inserted on the rack to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a team scored, a banner was placed on the rack to record it.

sentences.zh: 帝得籌，樂少止， 從官呼萬歲。

translations.literal: When the emperor scored, the music briefly stopped and attending officials cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor scored, the music briefly halted and attending officials shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 群臣得籌則唱好，得籌者下馬稱謝。

translations.literal: When ministers scored they cried approval; the scorer dismounted and expressed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers scored the crowd cried approval, and the scorer dismounted to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 凡三籌畢，乃禦殿召從臣飲。

translations.literal: When all three tallies were finished, he returned to the hall and summoned attending ministers to drink.
translations.idiomatic: After all three rounds were complete, he returned to the hall and summoned attending ministers to drink.

sentences.zh: 又有步擊者、乘驢騾擊者，時令供奉者朋戲以為樂雲。

translations.literal: There were also those who struck on foot and those who struck mounted on donkeys and mules; at times palace attendants formed teams for sport as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: There were also players on foot and players mounted on donkeys and mules; palace attendants sometimes formed teams for sport as entertainment.

sentences.zh: 救日伐鼓。

translations.literal: Rescuing the sun by beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: Rescuing the Sun: Beating Drums.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，司天監言日食五月朔，請掩藏戈兵鎧胄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, the Directorate of Astronomy reported an eclipse on the first day of the fifth month and requested that weapons, armor, and helmets be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianlong the Directorate of Astronomy reported an eclipse on the first day of the fifth month and requested that weapons, armor, and helmets be put away.

sentences.zh: 事下有司，有司請皇帝避正殿，素服，百官各守本司，遣官用牲太社如故事。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the responsible offices; they requested that the emperor withdraw from the main hall, wear plain dress, that all officials remain at their posts, and that officers be dispatched to offer victims at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the responsible offices, which requested that the emperor withdraw from the main hall and wear plain dress, that officials remain at their posts, and that envoys be dispatched to sacrifice at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 景德四年五月朔，日食。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month in the fourth year of Jingde, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month in the fourth year of Jingde there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上避正殿不視事。

translations.literal: The emperor withdrew from the main hall and did not conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew from the main hall and suspended audience with government business.

sentences.zh: 至和元年四月朔，日食，既內降德音：改元，易服，避正殿，減膳。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month in the first year of Zhihe there was a solar eclipse; an edict of grace was then issued from within: the reign title was changed, dress was altered, the main hall was avoided, and meals were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month in the first year of Zhihe there was a solar eclipse, whereupon an edict of grace was issued: the reign title was changed, court dress was altered, the emperor withdrew from the main hall, and meals were reduced.

sentences.zh: 百官詣東上閣門拜表請禦正殿，復常膳。

translations.literal: All officials went to the eastern upper Gate Secretariat, submitted memorials requesting that he resume the main hall, and restored regular meals.
translations.idiomatic: All officials went to the eastern upper Gate Secretariat and submitted memorials asking the emperor to resume audience in the main hall and restore regular meals.

sentences.zh: 三表乃從。

translations.literal: After three memorials he assented.
translations.idiomatic: Only after three such memorials did he assent.

sentences.zh: 至日，遣官祀太社，而陰雨以雷，至申， 乃見食，九分之餘。

translations.literal: On the day itself, officers were dispatched to sacrifice at the Great Altars; but with overcast rain and thunder, it was not until the shen hour that the eclipse was seen, with more than nine-tenths obscured.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself officers were dispatched to sacrifice at the Great Altars, but rain and thunder kept the sky overcast; not until the shen hour was the eclipse visible, with more than nine-tenths of the sun obscured.

sentences.zh: 百官稱賀。

translations.literal: All officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: All officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 先是皇祐初，以日食三朝不受賀，百官拜表。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Huangyou, because of the solar eclipse audiences were not held for three days and no congratulations were received; officials submitted memorials instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the beginning of the Huangyou reign, because of a solar eclipse the court held no congratulatory audiences for three days and officials submitted memorials instead.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年，詔正旦日食毋拜表，自十二月二十一日不御前殿，減常膳，宴遼使罷作樂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, an edict ordered that for the New Year's Day eclipse no memorials be submitted; from the twenty-first day of the twelfth month the front hall was not used, regular meals were reduced, the banquet for Liao envoys was cancelled, and music-making ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiayou an edict declared that for the New Year's Day eclipse no memorials need be submitted; from the twenty-first day of the twelfth month the emperor ceased holding court in the front hall, reduced his meals, cancelled the banquet for Liao envoys, and suspended music.

sentences.zh: 至日，仍遣官祀太社。

translations.literal: On the day itself, officers were still dispatched to sacrifice at the Great Altars.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself officers were still dispatched to sacrifice at the Great Altars.

sentences.zh: 百官三表，乃禦正殿，復膳。

translations.literal: After three memorials from all officials, he resumed the main hall and restored meals.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials from the officials he resumed audience in the main hall and restored regular meals.

sentences.zh: 六年六月朔日食，詔禮官驗詳典故。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month in the sixth year there was a solar eclipse; an edict ordered ritual officials to verify and examine precedents in detail.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month in the sixth year there was a solar eclipse, and an edict directed ritual officials to verify the relevant precedents.

sentences.zh: 皇帝素服，不禦正殿，毋視事，百官廢務守司。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain dress, did not use the main hall, did not conduct affairs, and all officials suspended business and remained at their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore plain dress, did not hold court in the main hall or conduct government business, and all officials suspended routine affairs and remained at their posts.

sentences.zh: 合朔前二日，郊社令及門僕 守四門，巡門監察鼓吹令率工人如方色執麾斿，分置四門屋下。

translations.literal: Two days before the new moon, the Director of the Suburban and Altar Rites and gate attendants guarded the four gates; the surveillance officer for gate patrol and the Director of Music led workers, each holding banners and pennants in the colors of their direction, and placed them beneath the buildings at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before the new moon, the Director of the Suburban and Altar Rites and gate attendants guarded the four gates; the gate-patrol surveillance officer and the Director of Music led workers holding direction-colored banners and pennants, placing them beneath the buildings at each gate.

sentences.zh: 龍蛇鼓隨設于左東門者立北塾南面，南門者立東塾西面，西門者立南塾北面，北門者立西塾東面。

translations.literal: Dragon-and-serpent drums were set accordingly: at the east gate on the left, standing at the north school facing south; at the south gate, at the east school facing west; at the west gate, at the south school facing north; at the north gate, at the west school facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-and-serpent drums were positioned accordingly: at the east gate, in the north schoolhouse facing south; at the south gate, in the east schoolhouse facing west; at the west gate, in the south schoolhouse facing north; and at the north gate, in the west schoolhouse facing east.

sentences.zh: 隊 正一人執刀，率衛士五人執五兵之器，立鼓外。

translations.literal: One squad leader holding a sword led five guardsmen bearing the five kinds of weapons and stood outside the drums.
translations.idiomatic: One squad leader with a sword led five guardsmen bearing the five kinds of weapons and stood outside the drums.

sentences.zh: 矛處東，戟處南，斧鉞在西，槊在北。

translations.literal: Spears were placed to the east, halberds to the south, axes and battle-axes to the west, and pikes to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Spears stood to the east, halberds to the south, axes and battle-axes to the west, and pikes to the north.

sentences.zh: 郊社令立於壇，四隅縈朱絲繩三匝。

translations.literal: The Director of the Suburban and Altar Rites set up a spear at the altar, and red silk cords were wound three times around the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Suburban and Altar Rites set up a spear at the altar, with red silk cords wound three times around the four corners.

sentences.zh: 又於北設黃麾，龍蛇鼓一次之，弓一、 矢四次之。

translations.literal: A yellow banner was also set up to the north; one dragon-and-serpent drum followed it, then one bow and four times as many arrows.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow banner was also set up to the north, followed by one dragon-and-serpent drum, one bow, and four sets of arrows.

sentences.zh: 諸兵鼓俱靜立，俟司天監告日有變，工舉麾，乃伐鼓；

translations.literal: All the weapon-bearers and drummers stood silently, waiting until the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the sun had changed; then the workers raised their banners and beat the drums;
translations.idiomatic: All the weapon-bearers and drummers stood in silence, waiting until the Directorate of Astronomy reported a change in the sun; then the workers raised their banners and beat the drums;

sentences.zh: 祭告官行事，太祝讀文，其詞以責陰助陽之意。

translations.literal: the sacrificial announcing officer performed the rite, and the chief invoker read the text, its words expressing the idea of reproving yin and assisting yang.
translations.idiomatic: the announcing officer performed the sacrifice while the chief invoker read the prayer, its words expressing the idea of reproving yin and assisting yang.

sentences.zh: 司天官稱止，乃罷鼓。

translations.literal: When the astronomy officer announced cessation, the drums were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the astronomy officer announced that the eclipse had ended, the drums fell silent.

sentences.zh: 如霿晦不見，即不伐鼓，自 是，日有食之，皆如其制。

translations.literal: If the sky was overcast and dark and it could not be seen, then drums were not beaten; from this time on, whenever there was a solar eclipse, all followed this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: If the sky was overcast and the eclipse could not be seen, drums were not beaten; thereafter, whenever there was a solar eclipse, the same regulations were followed.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，詔：“古者日食，百司守職，蓋所以祗天戒而備非常，今獨闕之，甚非王者小心寅畏之道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, an edict said: "In antiquity, at a solar eclipse the hundred offices kept their duties—this was to revere heaven's warning and guard against the unexpected; now this alone is lacking, which is very far from a king's careful, reverent way."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiping an edict declared: "In antiquity, when the sun was eclipsed the hundred offices kept to their duties, reverencing heaven's warning and preparing for the unexpected; that we now omit this alone is far from a ruler's careful reverence."

sentences.zh: 可令中書議舉行。

translations.literal: The Secretariat may be ordered to discuss and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Secretariat discuss and implement it.

sentences.zh: ”熙寧六年四月朔，日食，詔易服、避殿、減膳如故事。

translations.literal: " On the first day of the fourth month in the sixth year of Xining there was a solar eclipse; an edict ordered changing dress, avoiding the hall, and reducing meals according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " On the first day of the fourth month in the sixth year of Xining there was a solar eclipse, and an edict ordered altered dress, withdrawal from the hall, and reduced meals according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 降天下死刑，釋流以下罪。

translations.literal: Capital punishments throughout the realm were reduced, and crimes below exile were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Capital sentences throughout the realm were commuted and crimes below exile were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 政和上《合朔伐鼓儀》：有司陳設太社玉幣籩豆如儀。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe reign an edict presented the "Rite for Beating Drums at the New Moon": the responsible offices arranged jade, silk, baskets, and vessels at the Great Altars according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe reign regulations were issued for the "Rite for Beating Drums at the New Moon": officials set out jade, silk offerings, baskets, and vessels at the Great Altars according to ceremony.

sentences.zh: 社之四門，及壇下近北，各置鼓一，並植麾斿，各依其方色。

translations.literal: At the four gates of the altar and near the north below the mound, one drum was placed at each, and banners and pennants were planted, each in the colors of its direction.
translations.idiomatic: At each of the altar's four gates and near the north side below the mound, a drum was placed and banners and pennants were set up in the colors of their respective directions.

sentences.zh: 壇下立黃麾，麾杠十尺，斿八尺。

translations.literal: Below the mound a yellow banner was erected; its pole was ten chi and its pennant eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: Below the mound a yellow banner was erected on a ten-chi pole with an eight-chi pennant.

sentences.zh: 祭告日，於 時前，太官令帥其屬實饌具畢，光祿卿點視；

translations.literal: On the day of the sacrificial announcement, before the appointed hour, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led his subordinates to prepare the food offerings completely, and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments inspected them;
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the sacrificial announcement, before the appointed hour, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led his staff to prepare the food offerings, which the Minister of Imperial Entertainments inspected;

sentences.zh: 次引監察御史、奉禮郎、太祝、太官令先入就位，次引告官就位，皆再拜；

translations.literal: next the surveillance censor, ceremonial officer, chief invoker, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen were led in first to take their places, then the announcing officer was led to his place; all bowed twice;
translations.idiomatic: next the surveillance censor, ceremonial officer, chief invoker, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen were led in to take their places, then the announcing officer; all bowed twice;

sentences.zh: 次引御史、奉禮郎、太祝升，就位。

translations.literal: next the censor, ceremonial officer, and chief invoker ascended and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: next the censor, ceremonial officer, and chief invoker ascended and took their places.

sentences.zh: 太官令 就酌尊所，告官盥洗，詣太社三上香，奠幣玉，再拜復位。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen went to the wine vessel, the announcing officer washed his hands, proceeded to the Great Altars, offered incense three times, presented silk and jade, bowed twice, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen went to the wine vessel; the announcing officer washed his hands, proceeded to the Great Altars, offered incense three times, presented silk and jade, bowed twice, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 少頃，引告官再盥洗，執爵三祭酒，奠爵，俯伏興，少立，引太祝詣神位前跪讀祝文。

translations.literal: After a short while the announcing officer was led to wash his hands again, took the cup and offered wine three times, placed the cup, prostrated himself and rose, stood briefly, and the chief invoker was led before the spirit seat to kneel and read the prayer text.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the announcing officer washed his hands again, took the cup and poured libations three times, set down the cup, prostrated himself and rose, stood briefly, and the chief invoker was led before the spirit seat to kneel and read the prayer.

sentences.zh: 告官再拜退，伐 鼓。

translations.literal: The announcing officer bowed twice and withdrew, and drums were beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The announcing officer bowed twice and withdrew, and the drums were beaten.

sentences.zh: 其日時前，太史官一員立壇下視日。

translations.literal: Before the appointed hour on that day, one astronomy officer stood below the mound to watch the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointed hour that day, an astronomy officer stood below the mound to watch the sun.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令率工十人，如色服分立鼓左右以俟。

translations.literal: The Director of Music led ten workers, dressed in the colors of their directions, to stand left and right of the drums and wait.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music led ten workers in direction-colored dress to stand on either side of the drums and wait.

sentences.zh: 太史稱日有變，工齊伐鼓。

translations.literal: When the astronomy officer announced that the sun had changed, the workers all beat the drums together.
translations.idiomatic: When the astronomy officer announced a change in the sun, the workers beat the drums in unison.

sentences.zh: 明復，太史稱止，乃罷鼓。

translations.literal: When brightness returned, the astronomy officer announced cessation, and the drums were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun brightened again, the astronomy officer announced that the eclipse had ended, and the drums fell silent.

sentences.zh: 其日廢務，而百司各守其 職如舊儀。

translations.literal: On that day business was suspended, and the hundred offices each kept their duties according to the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: On that day routine business was suspended, and the hundred offices each remained at their posts according to the old regulations.

sentences.zh: ◎禮二十四

translations.literal: ◎ Rites 24
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Rites 24

sentences.zh: （軍禮）〉

translations.literal: (Military Rites)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Military Rites)〉

sentences.zh: ○祃祭閱武受降獻俘田獵打球救日伐鼓

translations.literal: ○ Ma sacrifice, military review, accepting surrender, presenting captives, field hunting, cuju ball game, rescuing the sun, beating drums
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ma sacrifice; military reviews; accepting surrender and presenting captives; field hunts; cuju; rituals to rescue the sun; and drum-beating

sentences.zh: 祃，師祭也，宜居軍禮之首。

translations.literal: Ma is the army sacrifice; it properly should stand first among military rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ma sacrifice was the army's ritual offering and rightly belonged at the head of military rites.

sentences.zh: 講武次之，受降、獻俘又次之。

translations.literal: Military exercises came next; accepting surrender and presenting captives came after that.
translations.idiomatic: Martial drills followed, with accepting surrender and presenting captives ranked after them.

sentences.zh: 田獵以下，亦各以類附焉。

translations.literal: Field hunting and below were likewise grouped by category.
translations.idiomatic: Field hunting and the rites below it were likewise arranged by kind.

sentences.zh: 軍前大旗曰牙，師出必祭，謂之祃。

translations.literal: The great banner before the army was called the ya; when the army set out it had to be sacrificed to—this was called ma.
translations.idiomatic: The main army banner was called the ya banner; whenever troops marched out they had to sacrifice to it, and this was called the ma rite.

sentences.zh: 後魏出師，又建纛頭旗上。

translations.literal: When the Later Wei sent out troops, they also erected a banner with a tassel head above it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Wei took the field they also set up a great standard topped with a tassel head.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，出京前一日，遣右贊善大夫潘慎修出郊，用少牢一祭蚩尤、祃牙；

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned in Hedong, on the day before leaving the capital he sent Right Assistant Gentleman Pan Shenxiu to the suburbs to offer one shao-lao sacrifice to Chiyou and to perform the ma rite for the ya banner;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Hedong, on the eve of his departure from the capital he sent Right Assistant Gentleman Pan Shenxiu outside the city to offer a shao-lao victim to Chiyou and perform the ma rite for the ya banner;

sentences.zh: 遣著作佐郎李巨源即北郊望氣壇用香、柳枝、燈油、乳粥、酥蜜餅、果，祭北方天王。

translations.literal: He sent Assistant Compiler Li Juyuan to the Qi-observation altar in the northern suburbs to offer incense, willow branches, lamp oil, milk porridge, honey cakes, and fruit in sacrifice to the Northern Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Assistant Compiler Li Juyuan to the qi-watching altar in the northern suburbs with incense, willow branches, lamp oil, milk porridge, honey cakes, and fruit to sacrifice to the Northern Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，詔太常禮院定祃儀。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, an edict ordered the Directorate of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix the ma rite.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping reign an edict directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to establish the ma ritual.

sentences.zh: 所司除地為壇，兩壝繞以青繩，張幄帟，置軍牙、六纛位版。

translations.literal: The responsible offices cleared ground for an altar, encircled it with two embankments bound with blue cord, hung curtains and canopies, and set up spirit tablets for the army ya and the six great banners.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cleared ground for an altar, ringed it with two embankments bound in blue cord, hung curtains and canopies, and set up spirit tablets for the army ya banner and the six great standards.

sentences.zh: 版方七寸，厚和三分。

translations.literal: The tablets were seven cun square and three fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The tablets were seven cun square and three fen thick.

sentences.zh: 祭用剛日，具饌。

translations.literal: Sacrifice was performed on a yang day, with food offerings prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice was performed on a yang day with full food offerings prepared.

sentences.zh: 牲用大牢，以羊豕代。

translations.literal: Victims were to be the great offering, but sheep and pigs were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: The prescribed victim was the great offering, but sheep and pigs were substituted.

sentences.zh: 其幣長 一丈八尺，軍牙以白，六纛以皂。

translations.literal: The silk offerings were one zhang and eight chi long; white for the army ya, black for the six great banners.
translations.idiomatic: The silk offerings were one zhang and eight chi long—white for the army ya and black for the six great banners.

sentences.zh: 都部署初獻，副都部署亞獻，部署三獻，皆戎服，清齋一宿。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief made the primary offering, the deputy commander the secondary, and a deployment commander the tertiary; all wore military dress and fasted in purification for one night.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief made the primary offering, the deputy commander the secondary, and a deployment commander the tertiary; all wore military dress and kept a night of ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 將校陪位。

translations.literal: Generals and officers attended in supporting places.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and officers stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 禮畢焚幣，釁鼓以一牢。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished the silk was burned and the drums smeared with blood from one victim.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended the silk offerings were burned and the drums anointed with blood from a single victim.

sentences.zh: 又擇日祭馬祖、馬社。

translations.literal: On another chosen day they sacrificed to the Horse Ancestor and the Horse Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day they also sacrificed to the Horse Ancestor and the Horse Altar.

sentences.zh: 閱武，仍前代制。

translations.literal: Military review still followed the institutions of earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Military reviews still followed the institutions of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗征伐四方，親講武事，故不盡用定儀，亦不常其處。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong campaigned in all directions and personally directed martial exercises, so they did not fully use the fixed ritual and did not keep to one place.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taizu and Taizong campaigned in every direction and personally directed martial drills, they did not always follow the fixed ritual and did not always hold reviews in the same place.

sentences.zh: 鑿講武池朱明門外以習水戰。

translations.literal: They cut a martial-exercise pool outside the Vermilion Bright Gate to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They excavated a drill pool outside the Vermilion Bright Gate to practice naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 復築講武台城西楊村，秋九月大閱，與從臣登臺觀焉。

translations.literal: They also built a martial-exercise terrace at Yang Village west of the city; in the ninth month of autumn they held a great review, and with their attending ministers they ascended the terrace to watch.
translations.idiomatic: They also built a drill terrace at Yang Village west of the city, and in the ninth month of autumn held a grand review at which they and their attending ministers mounted the terrace to watch.

sentences.zh: 真宗詔有司擇地含輝門外之東武村為廣場，馮高為台，臺上設屋，構行宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong ordered the responsible offices to choose ground at Dongwu Village outside the Splendid Radiance Gate as an open field, pile it high into a terrace, set a building on the terrace, and construct a traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong ordered officials to select ground at Dongwu Village outside the Splendid Radiance Gate as a parade ground, raise a high terrace, place a pavilion upon it, and build a traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 其夜三鼓，殿前、侍衛馬步諸軍分出諸門。

translations.literal: That night at the third drum the Palace Front and Imperial Guard horse and foot armies issued forth through the gates.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch the Palace Front and Imperial Guard horse and foot units marched out through the city gates.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，帝乘馬，從官並戎服，賜以窄袍。

translations.literal: At dawn the emperor mounted a horse; his attending officials all wore military dress and were granted narrow-sleeved robes.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor rode out on horseback; his attendants all wore military dress and were given narrow-sleeved robes.

sentences.zh: 至 行宮，諸軍陣台前，左右相向，步騎交屬亙二十裡，諸班衛士翼從于後。

translations.literal: Arriving at the traveling palace, the armies formed before the terrace facing one another left and right; foot and horse interlinked for twenty li; the various guard companies flanked and followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the traveling palace the armies formed before the terrace, facing one another on left and right, with infantry and cavalry interlinked for twenty li while the various guard companies flanked and followed behind.

sentences.zh: 有司奏成列，帝升台東向，禦戎帳，召從臣坐觀之。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported that the ranks were formed; the emperor ascended the terrace facing east, took his seat in a military tent, and summoned his attending ministers to sit and watch.
translations.idiomatic: When the responsible office reported that the ranks were formed, the emperor mounted the terrace facing east, took his seat in a military tent, and summoned his ministers to sit and watch.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使王超執五方旗以節進退， 又於兩陣中起候台相望，使人執旗如臺上之數以相應。

translations.literal: Palace Front Commander-in-Chief Wang Chao held the five-direction flags to regulate advance and retreat; signal platforms were also raised between the two formations facing one another, and men held flags matching those on the terrace to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Commander-in-Chief Wang Chao held the five-direction flags to regulate advance and retreat; signal platforms were also raised between the two formations, and men with flags matching those on the terrace coordinated the movements.

sentences.zh: 初舉黃旗，諸軍旅拜。

translations.literal: When the yellow flag was first raised, the armies bowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow flag was first raised, the armies bowed.

sentences.zh: 舉赤旗則騎進，舉青旗則步進。

translations.literal: Raising the red flag made the cavalry advance; raising the green flag made the infantry advance.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the red flag sent the cavalry forward; raising the green flag sent the infantry forward.

sentences.zh: 每旗動則鼓駴士噪，聲震百裡外，皆三挑乃退。

translations.literal: Whenever a flag moved the drums rolled and the soldiers shouted; the sound shook the countryside a hundred li away; each unit charged three times before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a flag moved the drums rolled and the soldiers shouted until the sound shook the countryside a hundred li away; each unit charged three times before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 次舉白 旗，諸軍復再拜，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Next the white flag was raised; the armies bowed again and shouted "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Next the white flag was raised; the armies bowed again and shouted "Long live the emperor."

sentences.zh: 有司奏陣堅而整，士勇而厲，欲再舉，詔止之，遂舉黑旗以振旅。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported that the formations were firm and orderly and the soldiers brave and sharp; they wished to raise the flags again, but an edict stopped them, and then the black flag was raised to dismiss the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office reported that the formations were firm and orderly and the soldiers brave and sharp; they wished to run another round, but the emperor ordered them to stop, and the black flag was raised to dismiss the troops.

sentences.zh: 軍于左者略右陣以還，由台前出西北隅；

translations.literal: The army on the left skirted the right formation to return and passed out through the northwest corner before the terrace;
translations.idiomatic: The army on the left skirted the right formation to return and marched out through the northwest corner before the terrace;

sentences.zh: 軍于右者略左陣以還，由台前 出西南隅，並凱旋以退。

translations.literal: the army on the right skirted the left formation to return and passed out through the southwest corner before the terrace; both withdrew in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: the army on the right skirted the left formation to return and marched out through the southwest corner before the terrace; both withdrew in triumph.

sentences.zh: 乃召從臣宴，教坊奏樂。

translations.literal: Then he summoned his attending ministers to a feast, and the Music Office performed.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned his ministers to a feast while the Music Office performed.

sentences.zh: 回禦東華門，閱諸軍還營，鈞容奏樂於樓下，復召從臣坐，賜飲。

translations.literal: Returning to the Eastern Flowery Gate, he reviewed the armies as they returned to camp; the Imperial Entertainers played music below the tower; he again summoned his attending ministers to sit and bestowed drink.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the Eastern Flowery Gate, he reviewed the armies as they returned to camp; the Imperial Entertainers played below the tower, and he again seated his ministers and bestowed drink upon them.

sentences.zh: 明日，又賜近臣飲於中書，諸軍將校飲于營中， 內職飲於軍器庫，諸班衛士飲于殿門外。

translations.literal: The next day he again bestowed drink on his close ministers at the Secretariat, on the army generals and officers in camp, on the inner service staff at the Armory, and on the various guard companies outside the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again bestowed drink on his close ministers at the Secretariat, on army generals and officers in camp, on inner-service staff at the Armory, and on the various guard companies outside the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 神宗閱左藏庫副使幵斌所教牌手於崇政殿，乃命殿前步軍司擇驍健者依法教習。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reviewed at the Chongzheng Hall the shield-bearers taught by Left Treasury Deputy Commissioner Bian Bin, and then ordered the Palace Front Foot Army Bureau to select the strongest men and train them according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong reviewed at the Chongzheng Hall the shield-bearers trained by Left Treasury Deputy Commissioner Bian Bin, then ordered the Palace Front Foot Army Bureau to select the strongest men and train them by the regulations.

sentences.zh: 自是，營屯及更戍諸軍、畿甸 三路民兵皆隨伎藝召見親閱焉。

translations.literal: From this time on, garrison troops, rotating frontier armies, and the three-circuit militia of the capital region were all summoned for personal review according to their skills.
translations.idiomatic: From then on garrison troops, rotating frontier armies, and the three-circuit militia of the capital region were all summoned for personal review according to their skills.

sentences.zh: 凡閱試禁衛、戍軍、民兵，總率第其精角，賜以金帛；

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial guards, frontier troops, and militia were reviewed and tested, their leaders were ranked by excellence and given gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial guards, frontier troops, and militia were reviewed, their leaders were ranked by excellence and rewarded with gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 而超等高者，至命為吏選官，其典領者優加職秩。

translations.literal: those of highest rank such as Chao were even appointed to office through clerk selection; those who commanded them received preferential advancement in rank.
